title: BEVerse: Unified Perception and Prediction in Birds-Eye-View for Vision-Centric Autonomous Driving
text: One shared BEV with ego-motion-aligned temporal fusion; detection, semantic map and motion decoders hang on it and a grid sampler gives each task its own range and cell size (nuScenes val: Tiny mAP 32.1 / NDS 46.6 / map IoU 48.7, Small 35.2 / 49.5 / 51.7). Template for a coarse detection grid next to a fine lane grid on one trunk. Blockers: Swin backbone and temporal stack are heavy, no loss-weighting recipe read, no FPS. Use the head layout only.

title: PETRv2: A Unified Framework for 3D Perception from Multi-Camera Images
text: Task-specific queries (detection, BEV segmentation, 3D lane) read one shared set of image tokens with temporal 3D position embeddings; state of the art claimed on all three, no numbers on the page read. Shows a trunk can be shared without a shared dense head. Blockers: multi-camera transformer, query heads, not a dense 0.5 m grid. Context only.

title: Cross-view Transformers for real-time Map-view Semantic Segmentation
text: Pretrained EfficientNet-B4 features (1/8 and 1/16) plus camera-aware cross-view attention onto a 200 x 200 map for 100 m x 100 m (0.5 m cells); about 4x faster than prior work, 45 FPS demo, MIT licence. A cheap camera-to-BEV baseline with a pretrained image backbone at exactly our grid. Blockers: vehicle and road classes only, coarse features hurt thin lane markings, no boxes. Use as the fast camera path to try first.

title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
text: Learns one loss weight per task so that each task's gradient norm at the last shared layer follows a common target scaled by its relative training rate; one hyper-parameter alpha; claims parity with grid search (rule from memory). Our shared layer would be the BEV feature map; cost is one extra backward per task through it. Blockers: dense thin-lane losses and sparse heatmap losses differ in scale by orders, no BEV result. Use as the second choice after uncertainty weighting.

title: Multi-Task Learning Using Uncertainty to Weigh Losses for Scene Geometry and Semantics
text: A learned noise parameter per task weighs the losses (about 1/(2 sigma^2) times the loss plus log sigma; form from memory); the joint depth plus segmentation model beats separate models. Zero-cost default for a lane segmentation head plus a heatmap detection head. Blockers: focal and Dice losses are not likelihoods, tends to down-weight the hard thin-structure task, so clamp the log-variance. Use first.

title: Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking (CenterPoint)
text: Objects are BEV centre peaks of a class heatmap; sub-cell offset, size, rotation and velocity are regressed at the peak, tracking by greedy closest-point matching on velocity (nuScenes lidar 65.5 NDS, 63.8 AMOTA). Sensor-independent anchor-free head on any 0.5 m BEV map and the detection head of BEVFusion and CRN; radar Doppler could supply velocity. Blockers: Gaussian radius for small objects at 0.5 m cells, no camera numbers. Use as the detection head.

title: CenterFusion: Center-based Radar and Camera Fusion for 3D Object Detection
text: CenterNet-style image detector with a frustum association of radar returns to object centres; radar features refine depth, rotation and velocity (NDS over the camera baseline by more than 12 percent; velocity improves without temporal input). The single-camera plus radar baseline for detection. Blockers: image-plane, rule-based association, old backbone. Context only.

title: Revisiting Birds Eye View Perception Models with Frozen Foundation Models: DINOv2 and Metric3Dv2
text: Frozen DINOv2 features in Lift-Splat-Shoot give +7.4 vehicle IoU on nuScenes with half the data and iterations; Metric3Dv2 depth as pseudo-lidar in Simple-BEV gives +3 IoU. Evidence that a frozen DINOv2 (small) front end transfers to BEV and saves trainable parameters. Blockers: workshop paper, no absolute IoU or latency on the page, patch stride 14 is coarse for thin lanes, Metric3Dv2 is heavy. Use as the case for a frozen ViT-S front end.

title: RepVGG: Making VGG-style ConvNets Great Again
text: Multi-branch training block re-parameterised to a plain 3x3 conv stack for inference; over 80 percent ImageNet top-1, 83 percent faster than ResNet-50 on a 1080Ti. Candidate for a conv-only BEV encoder or head that fuses to plain 3x3 layers. Blockers: no BEV or segmentation result, speed measured on an old GPU. Watch.

title: Fast-BEV: A Fast and Strong Bird's-Eye View Perception Baseline
text: Fixed-geometry voxel lift (pre-computed index, no depth head, no transformer), multi-scale image encoder, light BEV encoder, image plus BEV augmentation; R50 gives 52.6 FPS and 47.3 NDS on a 2080Ti against BEVDepth-R50 41.3 FPS and 47.5 NDS. Speed template for a one-camera system at fixed calibration. Blockers: detection only in the abstract, far range and thin structures blur without depth. Use the lift and the augmentation list.

title: FCOS3D: Fully Convolutional One-Stage Monocular 3D Object Detection
text: Per-pixel 3D targets (centre offset, depth, size, rotation), FPN-level assignment by 2D size and Gaussian centre-ness on the projected 3D centre; top camera entry of the NeurIPS 2020 nuScenes challenge. Monocular pretraining or auxiliary head recipe for the image features. Blockers: heavy ResNet-101 + DCN config, nuScenes numbers not read. Context only.

title: Multi-Task Learning as a Bargaining Game (Nash-MTL)
text: Per-task gradients at the shared parameters are combined by the Nash bargaining solution, with a convergence guarantee; claims state of the art on MTL benchmarks. Fallback if weighting fails to keep the lane head alive next to detection. Blockers: one backward per task, small gains in later benchmarks (memory). Watch.

title: MonoDETR: Depth-guided Transformer for Monocular 3D Object Detection
text: Foreground depth map plus depth encoder and a depth-guided decoder over learnable object queries; state of the art on KITTI. Only the auxiliary foreground-depth supervision transfers. Blockers: Hungarian matching, KITTI only. Context only.

title: GaussianLSS: Toward Real-world BEV Perception, Depth Uncertainty Estimation via Gaussian Splatting (CVPR 2025)
text: Per-pixel categorical depth (64 bins, 1-61 m) is reduced to mean and variance; the variance sets the extent of a 3D Gaussian (k = 0.5) that is alpha-blended into a 200 x 200 BEV at 0.5 m, rendered at 50/100/200 and fused. Six cameras, nuScenes val vehicle IoU 46.1 (448x800, visible) vs 47.6 for the projection-based PointBEV at 80 FPS vs 32 FPS and 0.33 vs 1.26 GiB; total 11.2 ms on an RTX 4090. Divider IoU 38.7. Never run with one camera; uncertainty = depth variance only.
idea: depth variance as splat footprint; multi-scale BEV render

title: MatrixVT: Efficient Multi-Camera to BEV Transformation for 3D Perception
text: Lift as one matrix multiplication with a precomputed sparse Feature Transporting Matrix; Prime Extraction (column-wise compression) plus Ring and Ray decomposition shrink it 30-50x; 112 categorical depth bins over 2-58 m. Map segmentation drivable 83.5 / lane 44.8 / vehicle 46.2 (6 cameras); 2-8x faster and up to 97% less memory than LSS, latency only plotted (no GPU named).
idea: FTM generated once; Gaussian sampling allowed in the matrix

title: BEVPoolv2: A Cutting-edge Implementation of BEVDet Toward Deployment
text: Skips the frustum feature tensor in LSS pooling with precomputed indices: view transformation 0.82 ms at 640x1600 (15.1x the previous fastest; GPU not named in the abstract). Engineering, categorical depth, abstract page only.
idea: precomputed pooling indices

title: Orthographic Feature Transform for Monocular 3D Object Detection (OFT)
text: Fixed 80 x 4 x 80 m voxel lattice at 0.5 m below the camera; each voxel average-pools the image features in its projected rectangle via an integral image, then height is collapsed with learned weights. No depth model, no ray distribution, no timing; KITTI car AP_BEV 8.79 (val moderate). Ancestor of Simple-BEV.
idea: voxel-to-pixel gather plus integral image

title: Cam2BEV: Sim2Real transformation of vehicle-mounted camera images to a semantically segmented BEV
text: Fixed IPM homographies as spatial transformers on encoder features (uNetXST, 9.6 M parameters); raw IPM image mIoU 30.2 vs 71.9 for the network (synthetic VTD data), showing how much a flat-ground warp loses for 3D objects and slopes. Single-front-camera variant exists. No timing.
idea: IPM as input prior plus learned correction

title: BEVHeight: A Robust Framework for Vision-based Roadside 3D Object Detection (CVPR 2023)
text: Predicts height above ground per pixel instead of depth, so with a known pose the lift is a fixed function of the height; roadside cameras only, abstract read, no numbers. The ground-prior-plus-residual idea.
idea: height over ground as the ray variable

title: MonoGround: Detecting Monocular 3D Objects from the Ground (CVPR 2022)
text: Ground plane as an extra depth source for monocular 3D detection; KITTI, no numbers on the abstract page.
idea: ground-plane depth prior

title: Translating Images into Maps (ICRA 2022)
text: Image column to BEV ray: a transformer translates each column (length h_u) into a radial sequence (polar w_u x r_u x C), resampled to a 100 x 100 Cartesian BEV at 0.5 m. nuScenes drivable 72.6 / car 37.4 / mean 25.0 (spatial model); monocular by design; no depth distribution and no speed.
idea: column-wise polar lift without depth

title: BEV-LaneDet: An Efficient 3D Lane Detection Based on Virtual Camera via Key-Points (CVPR 2023)
text: Monocular front camera: homography to a virtual camera, MLP view-relation module maps front-view features to a 200 x 40 BEV at 0.5 m; OpenLane F-score 58.4 vs 47.8; 185 FPS TensorRT / 102 FPS PyTorch on a V100. No depth uncertainty.
idea: virtual-camera warp then MLP lift

title: PanopticBEV: Bird's-Eye-View Panoptic Segmentation Using Monocular Frontal View Images
text: Monocular dense transformer: volumetric 3D-conv branch plus IPM with learned error correction; nuScenes mIoU 33.65 / road 77.3; 9.9 M parameters, about 240 ms per frame (GPU not read). Too slow; the flat branch is the useful part.
idea: IPM + learned correction for the road plane

title: GaussianFormer-2: Probabilistic Gaussian Superposition for Efficient 3D Occupancy Prediction (CVPR 2025)
text: Each Gaussian is the probability that its neighbourhood is occupied; geometry is the probabilistic product, semantics an exact Gaussian mixture; pixel-aligned occupancy initialisation; 8.9% of GaussianFormer's Gaussians. Abstract only, query-based refinement, six cameras.
idea: occupancy-probability superposition instead of depth-ordered blending

title: Focus on BEV: Self-calibrated Cycle View Transformation for Monocular BEV Segmentation
text: Monocular BEV segmentation, 29.2% mIoU nuScenes and 35.2% Argoverse (abstract only); mechanism and speed not read.
idea: monocular nuScenes reference number

title: RadarNet: Exploiting Radar for Robust Perception of Dynamic Objects (2020)
text: Lidar + radar. Early fusion rasterises radar clusters into a three-valued motion-aware occupancy (0 empty / 1 moving / -1 static); late fusion back-projects radial velocity onto the detected motion direction (v_r / cos phi) and a 5-layer MLP scores pairs with a no-association slot. nuScenes cars AVE -14 % for attention late fusion against -2 % for early fusion; AP +0.3 only. Shows how to use Doppler where it is geometrically meaningful and how to absorb clutter; needs lidar and boxes.

title: RC-BEVFusion: radar branch BEVFeatureNet for camera BEV detectors (2023)
text: Radar encoder for nuScenes 2+1D radar: 5 sweeps (300 ms), nine features per point (x y RCS v_d t_s plus offsets to pillar mean and pillar centre), 2000 non-empty cells x 10 points, PointNet with 32 channels, scatter, conv backbone. BEVDet camera only to camera + radar: NDS 0.411 -> 0.525, mAVE 0.918 -> 0.421, +17 ms on an RTX 2080 Ti. No per-attribute ablation. A copyable radar-encoder spec for a BEV grid.

title: Radar-Camera Pixel Depth Association for Depth Completion (CVPR 2021)
text: Radar hits are projected on an assumed ground-parallel plane; a U-Net predicts for each radar pixel which of 5 x 36 neighbouring pixels share its depth (height ambiguity, camera-radar baseline, occlusion), giving a 6-channel enhanced radar map for a depth completion net. nuScenes MAE image only 1.808 m, + raw radar 1.569 / 1.821, + enhanced radar 1.472 / 1.655; raw radar can even hurt. A learned footprint per radar point as an alternative to a fixed Gaussian; needs lidar-derived association labels.

title: RCM-Fusion radar-encoding detail: radar-guided BEV queries + gating + adaptive grid points (ICRA 2024)
text: Same paper as the SN40 row; this note adds the radar detail: PillarNet radar BEV (x y z RCS vx vy, 6 sweeps), radar-guided BEV queries and sigmoid gating (+6.7 NDS of the 8.0 total on a 1/7 subset), adaptive grid points around each radar point against position error (+0.5 NDS over no grid points, 52.4 -> 52.9). 2.3 FPS, 87.6 M parameters. Gating and guided queries portable; the rest heavy.

title: RCTrans: Radar-Camera Transformer via Radar Densifier and Sequential Decoder (AAAI 2025)
text: Radar points as 5 channels (xyz, compensated velocity, time offset; no RCS, argued against) into an MLP pillar encoder on 128 x 128 BEV, then a Radar Dense Encoder (1/2 - 1/8 scale, self-attention at the smallest scale, skips) fills the >90 % empty cells; radar elevation ambiguity handled by separate radar and image transformer stages. nuScenes val NDS / mAP: radar only 12.3 / 1.6, camera only 49.3 / 38.9, + radar 51.7 / 43.0, SECOND 55.1 / 46.6, dense encoder 56.4 / 48.2; full 58.6 / 50.9 at 52.2 ms (RTX 3090).

title: MVFusion: Semantic-aligned Radar and Camera Fusion for Multi-View 3D Detection (ICRA 2023)
text: Radar rendered per camera view as a 5-channel map (position mask, distance, RCS, radial velocity x and y; 3 m pillars) plus an image-derived foreground indicator, then a fusion transformer with radar + image queries and image-only keys. nuScenes val NDS 0.457 -> 0.475 (SARE +1.0, RGFT +0.8). The per-view radar image keeps viewing direction explicit (azimuth = column). Modest gain, weak PETR baseline, no attribute ablation.

title: RaCFormer: Query-based Radar-Camera Fusion (CVPR 2025)
text: Radar pillars (z = 0) give a radar BEV; radar points with a default height z_r = 1 are projected into the image to make a coarse radar depth map; discretised depth and RCS are embedded into the depth head (nuScenes val NDS 51.7 -> 52.9 with radar depth, 52.5 with RCS, 53.8 with both); a ConvGRU over multi-frame radar BEV (implicit dynamic catcher) gives mAP 43.4 -> 44.9 on fast objects. Light variant 64 x 64 grid at 1.6 m, 12 FPS RTX 3090, 58.8 NDS. The only recent paper that ablates RCS and depth separately.

title: RCBEVDet++: sparse fusion with RadarBEVNet, with BEV lane / drivable segmentation (2024)
text: RCS and Doppler speed per point; RCS-aware BEV encoder scatters each point into a radius set by RCS with a Gaussian-like weight (+1.4 NDS / +1.9 mAP, the largest single gain; transformer branch only +0.1 alone, 56.4 / 45.6 with injection-extraction), sparse camera queries sample the radar BEV. Segmentation (CVT-style decoder, classes vehicle / drivable / lane): 62.8 mIoU with R101, lane 50.5. No latency and no radar-off controlled segmentation comparison.

title: REDFormer: Radar Enlighten the Dark (T-IV 2024)
text: BEVFormer whose BEV queries come from a radar point-count saliency grid (embedding + gated unit); only the count per cell enters, no RCS or Doppler on the page. Night NDS 0.1913 -> 0.2812, rain 0.3877 -> 0.5091, but a rain / night multi-task head alone gives 0.2742 / 0.5060, so the radar share is small. Useful as an auxiliary-label trick for A8; needs a BEVFormer-class encoder.

title: RadarCam-Depth: Radar-Camera Fusion for Depth Estimation with Learned Metric Scale (ICRA 2024)
text: Radar gives metric scale to a monocular depth prediction: global scale alignment, learned quasi-dense scale from radar-patch association, local scale refinement; MAE 25.6 % lower than prior radar-camera depth methods on nuScenes (abstract only). Alternative to a lidar-supervised depth head for a front-camera BEV lift. Radar attributes not stated on the abstract page.

title: nuScenes radar point fields and devkit quirks (RadarPointCloud)
text: The loader has 18 fields including vx_comp / vy_comp (ego-compensated, recommended), rcs, ambig_state, dyn_prop, invalid_state and x_rms / y_rms / vx_rms / vy_rms (position and velocity error fields, unused by the papers). Default filters keep only invalid_state 0 and ambig_state 3. Multi-sweep merging transforms x y z only: velocity vectors are not rotated and the time lag is a separate array, so several radars with different yaw need the velocity rotated by hand.

title: SelfOcc: Self-Supervised Vision-Based 3D Occupancy Prediction (2023)
text: [F4] BEV or TPV features go through a two-layer MLP (per height slice for BEV) to an SDF, colour and optional semantics; neighbouring frames are rendered for a photometric and MVS depth loss with eikonal 0.1, Hessian 0.1 and sparsity 0.001 terms; occupancy at test time is the sign of the SDF with no rendering. Occ3D-nuScenes IoU 45.01 / mIoU 9.30 (TPV), 44.33 / 6.76 (BEV); SDF beat density for occupancy and depth but not for novel-view depth; 8x RTX 3090, 12 epochs. Weak absolute quality and heavy training; take the decoder and the eikonal / Hessian / sparsity regularisers (HTML read).

title: SurroundSDF: Implicit 3D Scene Understanding Based on Signed Distance Field (2024)
text: [F4] LSS voxels sampled at query points go through sine-activated MLPs to an SDF and semantics; the Sandwich Eikonal pushes the minimum SDF of occupied cells below zero and the SDF of free cells above zero, on top of lidar surface and eikonal terms. Occ3D-nuScenes val Small: occupancy baseline 38.33 mIoU, naive SIREN SDF 31.51, LODE 36.66, Sandwich Eikonal 40.52, plus joint loss 42.37 (Abs Rel 0.342 -> 0.174); keeps 41.07 at 10 % lidar and 40.16 at 1.6 m labels. A naive SDF is worse than occupancy; a good loss gains about 4 mIoU. Needs lidar-derived labels, no speed reported (HTML read).

title: UniOcc: Unifying Vision-Centric 3D Occupancy Prediction with Geometric and Semantic Rendering (2023)
text: [F4] Voxel features give density and semantic MLPs; depth (SILog against projected lidar) and semantics (cross-entropy against projected lidarseg) are rendered along Mip-NeRF-360 rays as an extra loss, weight 0.1 next to 3D labels, ~25,600 pixels per batch. BEVStereo R50 validation mIoU: 3D loss 19.6, rendering only 20.2, both 21.9; cumulative recipe 51.27 on the leaderboard (3rd). Rendering is additive to dense labels (+2 to +4 mIoU) and training-only; no geometric / semantic split, no speed (HTML read).

title: OccNeRF: Advancing 3D Occupancy Prediction in LiDAR-Free Environments (2023)
text: [F4] A contracted 300x300x24 volume predicts rendering weights directly (no density or SDF); depth of 3 frames per camera comes from photometric reprojection only (SSIM + L1, auto-mask), semantics from a prompted open-vocabulary segmenter. Occ3D-nuScenes mIoU 10.81; depth Abs Rel 0.202 against 0.627 for colour-difference only; contraction + resampling 0.216 -> 0.202; inference 0.18 s and 11 GB on an A100, 128 min per epoch on 8 A100. Cheap loss recipe, weak quality and slow for a 3060 (HTML read).

title: FlashOcc: Fast and Memory-Efficient Occupancy Prediction via Channel-to-Height Plugin (2023)
text: [F4] The head stays 2D: B x C x W x H BEV features become B x (C* Z) x W x H and are reshaped to B x C* x Z x W x H logits (channel-to-height); no 3D convs. Occ3D-nuScenes: BEVDetOcc 42.0 -> 43.3, UniOcc 45.2 -> 45.5 (rendering-supervised model stays compatible); BEV vs 3D conv 36.1 vs 37.8 / 39.2 vs 39.0 / 37.2 vs 37.3; BEV encoder + head 7.5 -> 3.1 ms, 398 -> 124 MiB; 210.6 FPS vs 92.1 FPS on RTX 3090 TensorRT FP16. Cheapest BEV to 3D lift; one SDF value per height bin would be the same reshape with C* = 1 (HTML read).

title: GaussianFormer: Scene as Gaussians for Vision-Based 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction (2024)
text: [F4] Sparse 3D semantic Gaussians refined by cross-attention and splatted to voxels (CUDA); loss CE + Lovasz per block; nuScenes SurroundOcc labels SC IoU 29.83 / SSC mIoU 19.10 with 144k Gaussians (SurroundOcc 31.49 / 20.30); 372 ms on an RTX 4090 and about 6.2 GB against 302-502 ms for voxel methods; 51k Gaussians 259 ms / 16.41 mIoU. A photometric rendering loss in the appendix did not help (16.24 vs 16.41). Memory saving only, not faster; negative evidence for pixel-photometric loss (HTML read).

title: GaussianOcc: Fully Self-supervised and Efficient 3D Occupancy Estimation with Gaussian Splatting (2024)
text: [F4] Voxel vertices are treated as Gaussians and splatted to depth and semantic maps instead of volume-rendered; stage 1 learns metric scale by splatting adjacent cameras with overlap masking; photometric SSIM + L1 losses, semantic weight 0.02. Rendering six surround images at 180x320 takes 0.17 s splatting against 0.85 s volume rendering (A100; volume rendering out of memory at 360x640, splatting unchanged), epochs 1 h vs 2.68 h; Occ3D-nuScenes self-supervised mIoU 9.94 (OccNeRF 9.54, SelfOcc 9.30); pretraining a supervised model +1.2 mIoU (37.29 to 38.45). Cheap rendering at equal quality (HTML read).

title: OccFlowNet: Towards Self-supervised Occupancy Estimation via Differentiable Rendering and Occupancy Flow (2024)
text: [F4] Volume rendering of an occupancy volume supervised only by lidar points projected to depth and semantic labels in the image (MSE + CE, 32,768 rays per frame, 50 + 100 samples, log class-frequency weights, 3 past and future frames). Occ3D-nuScenes val mIoU: semantics only 15.19, + depth 21.79, + temporal rendering 24.97, + dynamic filter and weights 26.14 (RenderOcc 23.93, 3D labels too 33.86 with flow); rendering is training-only. Depth and temporal rays carry the gain, class weighting is minor; 4 A100, no speed (HTML read).

title: A Simple Framework for 3D Occupancy Estimation in Autonomous Driving (2023)
text: [F4] 2D CNN, interpolation to a 256x256x16 grid and a 3D CNN give occupancy probabilities rendered to depth; SILog (0.85, 10) + BCE + L1, or photometric loss with SDF converted to density in the self-supervised case. DDAD Abs Rel: full 0.206, depth loss only 0.208, BCE only 0.221, L1 only 0.225; self-supervised nuScenes SDF 0.203 vs density 0.226. About 230 ms on an A100 (2D CNN 31, 3D CNN 101, rendering 95 ms; rendering skippable at inference). SILog depth rendering gives nearly all of the gain; SDF better than density by 10 % (HTML read).

title: MonoSDF: Exploring Monocular Geometric Cues for Neural Implicit Surface Reconstruction (2022)
text: [F4] Neural SDF volume rendering with L = L_rgb + 0.1 eikonal + 0.1 depth (scale-and-shift aligned in closed form) + 0.05 normal. Replica MLP Chamfer-L1 / F-score: no cues 6.75 / 66.88, depth 4.26 / 76.42, normal 3.19 / 85.84, both 2.94 / 86.18; depth predictor quality moves F-score from 68.6 (MiDaS) to 86.7 (Omnidata). Per-scene optimisation (6-11 h on an RTX 3090) on indoor scenes, so take the loss recipe only, not the pipeline (HTML read).

title: GaussianBeV: 3D Gaussian Representation meets Perception Models for BeV Segmentation (2024)
text: [F4] Per-pixel 3D Gaussians (metric depth from disparity, offset, allocentric rotation) are splatted orthographically to a 200x200 BEV (50 cm cells), then a BEV backbone; losses segmentation, log-depth and early supervision on the rasteriser output. Vehicle IoU with a backbone 46.7 - 47.3 per variant, full 47.5 (LSS) / 47.0 (Simple-BEV): depth loss and early supervision give nothing alone, a little together; 24 fps (224x448) on an A100. Small effect of a depth loss on a strong BEV backbone; same lifting family as our SN01 (HTML read; table partly garbled).

title: Tri-Perspective View for Vision-Based 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction (TPVFormer) (2023)
text: [F4] Adds two vertical feature planes to BEV; the feature of a 3D point is the sum of its three plane projections, lifted from images by attention and trained with sparse lidar supervision. SC IoU 30.86 / SSC mIoU 17.10 on SurroundOcc labels, 341 ms latency copied from another table; in SelfOcc the TPV decoder gives mIoU 9.30 against 6.76 for plain BEV. The tri-plane decoder costs O(HW + HZ + WZ), a cheap height lift between BEV and voxels (abstract page read; numbers from other papers read).

title: BEVDet4D: Exploit Temporal Cues in Multi-camera 3D Object Detection
text: Warps the previous BEV feature by the ego transform (bilinear, rotation plus translation), concatenates it with the current one, adds a two-unit BEV encoder, and turns velocity into the positional offset between the two aligned features. nuScenes val Tiny: 39.2 to 44.0 NDS, mAVE 0.909 to 0.479 (0.328 with rotation, time-gap augmentation); an unaligned concatenation is worse than no history (37.6 NDS). Temporal part costs +1 M parameters, +7 GFLOPs, 15.6 to 15.5 FPS; aligning after the view transform is 2x faster than inside. For us the cheapest two-frame static memory; moving objects are only implicit in the feature difference.
extract: skip: scan level note is enough

title: Time Will Tell (SOLOFusion): long-term low-res BEV history plus short-term stereo
text: Stacks ego-aligned BEV maps of 16 past frames at 1/16 resolution into a cost volume and adds high-resolution plane-sweep stereo against the previous frame. nuScenes val: 0 / 1 / 16 / 41 past frames give NDS 0.347 / 0.423 / 0.474 / 0.467, so it saturates at 16; both streams 11.4 FPS, 3.6 GB against 17.6 FPS, 3.3 GB baseline. Parallel stacking grows with the window and has only ego warp for moving objects. For us: coarse long memory plus fine current frame; the stereo part needs a trainable image backbone.

title: VideoBEV: Exploring Recurrent Long-term Temporal Fusion for Multi-view 3D Perception
text: One recurrent BEV memory: H_i = [warp(H_i-1, ego); B_i] * V with a conv V that down-weights older frames, plus a time-gap embedding fused the same way for the velocity head. nuScenes val: history 0 / 1 / 4 / 16 / all gives NDS 0.382 / 0.450 / 0.471 / 0.489 / 0.492, mAVE 0.936 to 0.331; at 50 percent missed frames the time embedding removes 25 percent of the velocity error rise. Constant memory (one BEV map), overhead near the no-history model per a figure (no numbers in text). No moving-object gate. Template for our static hold with a learned decay.

title: BEVFormer: spatiotemporal transformers for BEV from multi-camera images
text: Temporal self-attention: previous BEV shifted by ego motion, deformable attention over queries and aligned history with offsets predicted from their concatenation, recurrent at test time. nuScenes val: 0.517 NDS / 0.416 mAP against 0.448 / 0.375 spatial-only, mAVE 0.802 to 0.394; ego alignment itself only +0.007 NDS. Latency 130 ms (6 layers), 25 ms (1 layer), 7 ms (single scale, 100 x 100 BEV, 1 layer), no temporal-only figure. The deformable offsets absorb object motion without a flow head; the cheaper descendants are VideoBEV and MemFusionMap.

title: RLG-TPV: Radar- and LiDAR-Guided Tri-Perspective View Fusion for Camera-Radar 3D Detection
text: Doppler-guided temporal fusion aligns past fused features with a motion field phi = s * Smooth(v_radar) + learned residual, gated by sigmoid((speed - tau_v)/T) so cells without measured motion get no extra warp; occupancy gate on weak features; four keyframes at 1 s. nuScenes val 0.4981 mAP / 0.5959 NDS; the DGTF block adds +0.0013 mAP / +0.0040 NDS, which the authors call within noise; one keyframe instead of four costs -11.5 percent mAP. No cost figures, no code, ego compensation of Doppler unspecified. Gate form is the transferable part.

title: 4DR360: State Reasoning for Joint 3D Detection and Occupancy Prediction in 4D Radar-Camera Perception
text: Doppler-guided temporal fusion caches state, occupancy, pose and a BEV motion field of the last frames; ego alignment, then a dynamic warp by clipped velocity from the decoded velocity map corrected with radar Doppler, confidence-weighted decay average, residual Conv3D update. ManTruckScenes 4 frames: no temporal 47.45 mAP / 50.89 NDS, ego align only 47.12 / 50.45 (below no history), state memory 49.06 / 52.28, plus Doppler warp 49.57 / 52.97, mAVE 1.0213 to 0.9442. Whole model 4.5 - 5.5 FPS, no DTF-specific cost. Shows ego warp alone does not help and the Doppler warp is a second-order gain.

title: AttentiveGRU: Recurrent Spatio-Temporal Modeling for Radar-Based BEV Object Detection
text: Radar BEV memory buffer fused with the present frame by 32 latent queries per block (3 blocks, width 64), median-thresholded cross-attention gates, 1x1 conv gates on overlaps and a deformable conv for non-overlap regions; no ego pose input. nuScenes car class: 32.4 to 39.2 mAP (+21 percent relative) with CenterPoint Transformer, gains largest for moving classes, weaker for large stationary vehicles. T=2 on nuScenes, one 2080Ti, no cost or ablation numbers. Co-authored by the user (Meuter). Ego-free alignment is weaker than an exact warp when the pose is known.

title: Redefining Radar Segmentation: Static-Moving Segmentation and Ego-Motion Estimation from Radar Point Clouds
text: Per-point MLP + GRU over 8 raw radar scans gives static and moving probabilities; static returns follow a sine relation of radial velocity and azimuth, a weighted least-squares fit gives sensor velocity and re-weights the static set. RadarScenes: moving IoU 0.86, F1 0.92; ego RMSE 0.37 cm/s (vx), 0.12 deg/s (yaw rate); 0.15 M parameters. With our known ego velocity the expected static Doppler is a closed formula, so a moving mask needs no network. Not shown on nuScenes radar; no code.

title: MotionNet: Joint Perception and Motion Prediction from BEV Maps
text: Five ego-aligned LiDAR sweeps as 13 x 256 x 256 occupancy, a pyramid network with pseudo-1D temporal convs, per-cell class, 1 s motion and static probability; motion zeroed on background and on static foreground. nuScenes LiDAR: motion error static 0.026 m, slow 0.257 m, fast 1.074 m; ego sync matters (0.257 to 0.425 without); 19 ms per inference. Background temporal-consistency loss across ego-aligned frames is a label-free signal for the static part. LiDAR input, bicycles weak.

title: FIERY: Future Instance Prediction in Bird's-Eye View from Surround Monocular Cameras
text: Camera BEV on 200 x 200 at 0.5 m, past states warped by a spatial transformer with ego-motion as extra channels, 3D-conv temporal model (64 x 200 x 200 state), ConvGRU for the future, heads for centerness, offset, segmentation and flow, instances linked by flow-warped centers. nuScenes 2 s: IoU 59.4 / 36.7, VPQ 50.2 / 29.9 against a static model 47.9 / 30.3 and 43.1 / 24.5; about 8.1 M parameters, no inference latency. The recipe at our grid size; instance flow is the moving-object handle; future prediction out of scope.

title: MemFusionMap: Working Memory Fusion for Online Vectorized HD Map Construction
text: Fixed-lag buffer of 4 ego-warped BEV frames plus a warped overlap heatmap (cell age, start all ones, +1 per step) turned into 32 channels, fused with a dilated conv block and LayerNorm. nuScenes mAP against StreamMapNet 34.1 to 38.0 (60 x 30 m) and 22.2 to 27.6 (100 x 50 m); 15.1 against 15.3 FPS. Static map content only, no moving-object path. The age channel and bounded memory are cheap and transfer to a lane BEV memory.

title: Probably Unknown: Deep Inverse Sensor Modelling Radar (ICRA 2019)
text: Raw polar FMCW scan (azimuth x range power) goes through a polar encoder and a Cartesian U-Net decoder with Polar Transformer Units (bilinear polar-to-Cartesian resampling); per cell it predicts a logit mean and a variance, p = sigmoid(mu / sqrt(1 + (gamma sqrt(pi/8))^2)). Lidar ray-traced partial labels; observed cells get BCE over 25 samples, unobserved cells a KL to the prior, partial cells no loss. Own 5 h urban set: occupied IoU 0.35 vs CFAR 0.24 / 0.20, mean 0.63 vs 0.50 / 0.55; high variance marks occluded space; 14 Hz at 600 x 600 on a Titan Xp. Scanning radar without Doppler; not nuScenes.
idea: per-cell predicted variance as learned confidence; polar-to-Cartesian bilinear layer; observed / unobserved loss split

title: Deep Radar Inverse Sensor Models for Dynamic Occupancy Grid Maps
text: Sparse detections of one radar become a binary polar map (300 azimuth x 350 range bins, 0.36 deg x 0.2 m); a DANet segments it into free / occupied / unknown evidential masses on the polar grid; Dice loss; lidar ray-traced DGM labels; applied per sensor. Highway, six SRR 520: mounting change A to B front-centre mIoU 68.70 to 63.52; P(occupied | true occupied) 38.68 vs 15.30 for a Gaussian-mixture geometric ISM. Doppler and RCS unused as input; no runtime or code.
idea: learned polar footprint of sparse detections replacing a hand-set Gaussian; per-sensor application

title: Road Scene Understanding by Occupancy Grid Learning from Sparse Radar Clusters using Semantic Segmentation (ICCVW 2019)
text: nuScenes radar clusters (up to 128 per radar) rasterised to a binary 215 x 50 grid at 0.4 m in the radar frame, 1 / 10 / 20 ego-compensated frames; U-Net with Lovasz-softmax predicts occupied / free / unobserved from lidar ray-traced labels. Test mIoU: Delta ISM 0.244, Gaussian ISM 0.223, ray trace 0.349, network 0.439; occupied IoU only 0.108; 20-frame aggregation +16.7 % over one frame. Dynamic clusters removed; no runtime.
idea: learned replacement of the Gaussian inverse sensor model on nuScenes radar with an unobserved class

title: Radar Occupancy Prediction with Lidar Supervision while Preserving Long-Range Sensing and Penetrating Capabilities
text: U-Net on the polar range-azimuth image of a scanning radar (Navtech 4 Hz) trained only within 52.5 m where lidar labels exist (400 x 300 crops), applied by a sliding window with stride 10.5 m over the full range; Tversky loss. Polar training gives an average IoU 4.2 times that of Cartesian training outside the training range (as stated); radar odometry translation error 0.0783 to 0.0528 m/frame. No uncertainty, no runtime.
idea: polar images make a range-trained network extend to far range

title: RadarOcc: Robust 3D Occupancy Prediction with 4D Imaging Radar (NeurIPS 2024)
text: Raw 4D radar tensor (256 x 107 x 37 x 64, K-Radar): 8-channel Doppler descriptor, top-250-per-range-bin sparsification, range-wise attention, spherical sparse-conv encoder, deformable cross-attention from Cartesian queries to spherical reference points, 128 x 128 x 14 grid at 0.4 m. IoU 48.8 / 39.1 / 30.4 at 12.8 / 25.6 / 51.2 m; spherical encoding adds 2.6 / 0.7 / 1.0 IoU; per-range sparsification matters most (mIoU 34.3 to 24.1 without); 302.9 ms on a GTX 3090. Raw tensor and speed out of reach.
idea: keep radar polar until the last step; per-range-bin top-k instead of a global threshold

title: A Resource Efficient Fusion Network for Object Detection in Bird's-Eye View using Camera and Raw Radar Data (ITSC 2024)
text: Front camera warped by fixed geometry to BEV and then to a polar range-azimuth grid; radar RD tensor encoded to RA features; channel concatenation fusion; heads on a 128 x 224 polar grid (0.8 m x 0.8 deg) with occupancy plus range / azimuth offset regression. RADIal test: AP 95.75 %, AR 91.35 %, range error 0.11 m, angle error 0.09 deg, 6.58 M parameters, 58.91 FPS. Vehicles only, raw radar required.
idea: fixed camera-to-polar warp and polar fusion in a front-view setup

title: Raw High-Definition Radar for Multi-Task Learning (FFT-RadNet / RADIal, CVPR 2022)
text: Range-Doppler input (512 x 256 x 32) to a range-angle decoder; detection on a 0.8 m x 0.8 deg polar map with a sigmoid occupancy map plus range / azimuth offset regression (focal + smooth-L1) and free-space segmentation (BCE). RADIal test IoU 0.5: AP 96.84 %, AR 82.18 %, range error 0.11 m, angle error 0.17 deg; Pixor on the point cloud has recall 32.32 %; 3.79 M parameters, 584 GFLOPS. No predicted variance.
idea: polar cell + offset code for a position; recall lost by point-only radar

title: RADDet: Range-Azimuth-Doppler based Radar Object Detection for Dynamic Road Users
text: 256 x 256 x 64 RAD tensor to a ResNet-style backbone; 3D YOLO head on the polar RAD grid and a 2D head after a learned polar-to-Cartesian coordinate transformation layer (channel-wise FC). AP 0.563 at IoU 0.3 (3D) and 0.516 at IoU 0.5 (2D); about 10 k frames, sunny only; no polar vs Cartesian ablation.
idea: learned polar-to-Cartesian layer (we prefer a fixed table)

title: Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural Radiance Fields
text: Casts a cone per pixel (radius = pixel width x 2/sqrt(12)) and replaces each ray sample by the Gaussian (mean, covariance) of the conical frustum between t0 and t1 in closed form; integrated positional encoding damps frequencies finer than the frustum. Multiscale Blender error about 60 % lower than NeRF, 7 % faster, 612 k vs 1191 k parameters. The maths of a pixel-group footprint: marginalise the Gaussian to the BEV xy block for an anisotropic footprint that grows with range. Rendering paper, no driving result.
idea: cone footprint as closed-form Gaussian per (cell; depth bin)

title: Zip-NeRF: Anti-Aliased Grid-Based Neural Radiance Fields
text: Grid lookup with a cone: six hexagonal multisamples per frustum, each an isotropic Gaussian, and the lookup at grid level l scaled by erf(1/sqrt(8 sigma^2 n_l^2)) so wide Gaussians contribute less. 8-77 % lower error than mip-NeRF 360 / iNGP baselines, 24x faster training than mip-NeRF 360. The erf factor is the mass of a Gaussian inside one grid cell: the per-cell integral for a BEV footprint (scout inference). No 2D or driving use; no official repo seen.
idea: erf downweighting of a footprint against the grid cell
code: not on the abstract page (project page jonbarron.info/zipnerf)

title: Lift, Splat, Shoot: Encoding Images from Arbitrary Camera Rigs by Implicitly Unprojecting to 3D
text: Per-pixel context x depth probability over about 42 fixed depths (4-45 m, 1 m), one point per (pixel; bin), sum-pooled into the nearest cell of a 200 x 200 BEV at 0.5 m by a cumsum trick with analytic gradient; 35 Hz on a Titan V. nuScenes car IoU 32.06 vs OFT 29.72; drivable 72.94, lane boundary 19.96. The point lift that a cone footprint would replace. Code under the NVIDIA Source Code License: research and evaluation only, so re-implement.
idea: nearest-cell point splat (baseline of the cone lift)

title: BEVDepth: Acquisition of Reliable Depth for Multi-view 3D Object Detection
text: Camera-aware DepthNet (intrinsics/extrinsics MLP as SE gate), lidar depth BCE on min-pooled projected points, depth refinement module (+0.8 mAP), one-thread-per-feature CUDA voxel pooling (80x faster than LSS pooling). nuScenes val R50 256x704 35.1 mAP / 47.5 NDS; test 60.0 NDS with TTA. Text and table disagree on the total gain on the page read. Still a point lift; the depth-supervision recipe stays under a cone lift.
idea: camera-aware depth gate; lidar depth loss

title: CaDDN: Categorical Depth Distribution Network for Monocular 3D Object Detection (full method + OpenPCDet code)
text: Update of the abstract-only row. LID depth bins, frustum G = depth distribution outer product with 64-channel stride-4 features, voxel-centric trilinear sampling of G into X x Y x Z x C, Z folded into channels and a 1x1 conv to BEV, PointPillars-style head; focal depth loss alpha_fg 3.25 / alpha_bg 0.25. KITTI test Car 19.17 / 13.41 / 11.46; val ablation: no depth supervision 5.66 vs 14.03, LID 16.31 vs uniform 15.10, full distribution 16.31 vs one-hot 13.71. Dense volume is heavy; the voxel-centric lookup is a fixed small footprint.
idea: voxel-centric frustum lookup; LID bins; foreground-weighted depth focal loss

title: GaussianCaR: Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Camera-Radar Fusion (ICRA 2026)
text: Camera pixels (stride 8; depth-bin logits, offset, size from depth-distribution std x 0.5, opacity, 128-d feature) and radar points (PTv3, 7 sweeps, offset, free 6-value covariance, opacity) all become Gaussians alpha-blended into a 200 x 200 BEV at 0.5 m. nuScenes vehicle IoU 57.3, road 82.9, divider 50.1; 75.6 ms on an RTX 4090 vs BEVCar 245.6 ms. Radar scatter 56.1 vs Gaussians 56.9; sweeps 1 / 4 / 7: 54.9 / 56.2 / 57.3. No pixel cone, no range-azimuth radar model, no dt.
idea: one splat interface for camera and radar

title: Deep Parametric Continuous Convolutional Neural Networks (CVPR 2018)
text: Layer h_i = sum_j g(y_i - x_j) f_j with the kernel g an MLP of the continuous relative offset; output points need not equal input points; KNN or radius window; weight tensor factorised for speed. Lidar segmentation 94.56 pACC / 46.35 mIoU at 9.34 MB vs 74.66 MB for 3D-FCN. The formal template of a learned density at BEV cells as a function of the offset to a detection; the offset would be taken in polar sensor coordinates and conditioned on r_d, features, dt (the paper conditions on the offset only).
idea: learned kernel of relative offset; dense output from sparse input

title: Deep Continuous Fusion for Multi-Sensor 3D Object Detection (ContFuse; ECCV 2018)
text: Each BEV pixel gathers its K nearest lidar points, samples the image feature at each projection and sums MLP([feature; 3D offset to the pixel]); KITTI test Car BEV moderate AP 85.83 at about 0.06 s; offset input matters (removing it hurts), K = 1 as good as K = 3. BEV-cell-centric gather with the geometry as MLP input; lidar-dense, no radar, Cartesian offsets.
idea: cell-centric gather over neighbours; offset as MLP input

title: KPConv: Flexible and Deformable Convolution for Point Clouds (ICCV 2019)
text: Kernel = K kernel points with linear influence max(0; 1 - d/sigma) and weights W_k over a radius neighbourhood; deformable offsets predicted per location with fitting and repulsive regularisers. S3DIS Area-5 mIoU 65.4 rigid / 67.1 deformable; ScanNet 68.6 / 68.4. A compact, compactly supported g for a radar density (a few learned lobes in range-azimuth); no radar or driving evidence, dense-cloud design.
idea: structured kernel with few learned lobes; compact support

title: PointPillars: Fast Encoders for Object Detection from Point Clouds (CVPR 2019) + OpenPCDet
text: 9-feature point decoration (offsets to pillar mean and centre), linear-BN-ReLU-max pillar encoder, scatter to a pseudo-image; 62 Hz (16 ms on a 1080 Ti, encoder 1.3 ms). OpenPCDet nuScenes config: 0.2 m pillars, 20 points, 30000 pillars, 64 filters, five point features incl. timestamp, 10 sweeps. The hard-binning baseline with the dt channel already in the features; the learned density replaces the hard assignment.
idea: hard pillar baseline with timestamp feature

title: TransCAR: Transformer-based Camera-And-Radar Fusion for 3D Object Detection
text: Radar: 5 accumulated sweeps, 18 nuScenes channels plus one time-offset channel (36 after one-hot), position MLP with M = 1500 points; cross-attention learns the radar-query association. Val NDS with 0 / 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 sweeps 42.2 / 44.3 / 44.9 / 46.4 / 46.3; removing velocity mAVE 0.523 to 0.906; no ablation of the time offset. Test 42.2 mAP / 52.2 NDS vs DETR3D 41.2 / 47.9. Evidence that dt is a plain point channel, not a tested one.
idea: time offset as a point channel; sweep curve saturating at 5

title: BEVCar: Camera-Radar Fusion for BEV Map and Object Segmentation (IROS 2024)
text: Voxel-grid radar encoder (xyz, uncompensated vx vy, RCS; 5 sweeps; no dt), radar-guided deformable attention initialises the BEV queries of the image lift. nuScenes val vehicle 58.4, drivable 83.3, lane 45.3; radar-guided lift vs parameter-free lift +1.8 vehicle / +4.2 map mIoU, learned radar encoder vs raw metadata +0.6 / +0.9. 137-382 ms on an A100. Radar as a prior over where along the ray the camera mass goes. Code non-commercial.
idea: radar prior steering the camera lift

title: Simple-BEV: What Really Matters for Multi-Sensor BEV Perception?
text: Parameter-free lift (mechanism from memory: voxel centres projected into the feature map and sampled bilinearly) plus radar rasterised into the BEV; batch size and resolution matter more than the lifting method. README: camera + radar mean IoU 55.8 vs camera-only 47.6 on trainval (definition not on the page). Strong simple baseline and control for any cone-lift claim; 18 ms class speed (from the BEVCar table).
idea: parameter-free point-sampling lift as control

title: Mip-Splatting: Alias-free 3D Gaussian Splatting
text: 3D filter limits Gaussian size to the sampling frequency of the training views, a 2D Mip filter (box filter simulating pixel integration) replaces the screen-space dilation. Abstract page only; no numbers. The footprint rule for Gaussian splats that GaussianLSS and GaussianCaR lack (a Gaussian below one 0.5 m cell aliases); formulas to be read before use.
idea: cell-sized box filter on the splat covariance
code: project page niujinshuchong.github.io/mip-splatting (no repo on abstract page)

title: DualBEV: Unifying Dual View Transformation with Probabilistic Correspondences (ECCV 2024)
text: HeightTrans: 13 fixed heights per BEV cell are projected, the image feature is sampled bilinearly and multiplied by P_proj, the per-pixel depth distribution read by a trilinear grid sampler (depth as third axis), then summed; table plus BEVPoolV2 operator. nuScenes val ablation: without P_proj 27.0 / 40.0 mAP / NDS vs 37.0 / 48.8 with it (multi-frame); on a BEVDet base Prob-Sampling 30.6 / 39.0 at 0.32 ms vs unweighted bilinear sampling 30.5 / 37.6 at 7.15 ms and SCA_da 29.5 / 36.6 at 12.50 ms (one RTX 3090; resolution not stated). Detection only, no segmentation.
idea: pull at fixed heights times depth probability at the point's own depth

title: FastBEV++: Fast by Algorithm Deployable by Design
text: View transform as Index-Gather-Reshape in standard operators (TensorRT-native, no custom plugin); depth-aware step F = Gather(F_img) times Gather(D_prob) with a depth head trained only through the detection loss. nuScenes val R50 0.344 mAP / 0.478 NDS camera-only, 0.359 / 0.488 with depth fusion (R101 NDS 0.507 -> 0.522); 134 FPS INT8 on a Tesla T4 (whole network); abstract and text disagree on 0.359 NDS vs mAP. D_prob shape and bins not defined on the page read.
idea: gather feature times gathered depth probability; pure-gather TensorRT export

title: FB-BEV: BEV Representation from Forward-Backward View Transformations (ICCV 2023)
text: Forward (LSS) BEV plus backward spatial cross-attention on foreground-proposed cells; the backward part is weighted by a depth-consistency weight w_c = interpolated bin vector dot the pixel's depth distribution (118 bins, 1 m start, 0.5 m step). Depth-aware vs not: BEVFormer 0.379 -> 0.387 NDS, FB-BEV 0.397 -> 0.406; view transform 2.6 / 3.4 / 6.6 ms at BEV 128 / 256 / 400 vs BEVDet 0.7 / 0.8 / 1.5 ms (GPU not named); test 62.4 NDS. Detection only; code NVIDIA research-only.
idea: depth-consistency weight at the point's own depth inside a backward lift

title: DFA3D: 3D Deformable Attention For 2D-to-3D Feature Lifting (ICCV 2023)
text: Deformable attention in the (u, v, depth) volume D (x) X without materialising it: trilinear sampling split into a depth-score interpolation and a depth-weighted bilinear gather. BEVFormer-base 41.6 / 51.7 -> 43.0 / 53.1 mAP / NDS; lidar ground-truth depth 56.7 / 62.4; equivalent implementation 29 MB and 5.2 ms vs 3204 MB and 161.9 ms for the naive volume (GPU not named). Slower end to end (2.4 FPS); the id in the scout brief (2307.04337) was wrong.
idea: depth-weighted gather without the frustum tensor; depth oracle gain

title: PointBeV: A Sparse Approach to BeV Predictions
text: Sparse Feature Pulling: pillar of heights per BEV point, only the cameras that see it, bilinear gather, camera average, coarse-to-fine sparse points; no depth weight. nuScenes 224 x 480: vehicle 38.1 / 44.0 IoU, pedestrian 18.5 / 19.9, lane 49.6; pull module 1.9 ms vs 4.3 ms forward on six cameras (GPU not named), 14.84 vs 13.70 FPS at batch 1. The depth-free null and plain-PyTorch code for lift P.
idea: visibility-masked pull and sparse coarse-to-fine cells

title: FisheyeGaussianLift: BEV Feature Lifting for Surround-View Fisheye Camera Perception
text: Per-pixel Gaussian from a fisheye ray LUT times 64 depth-bin centres (1-30 m), covariance sigma^2 I + Delta Delta^T with the depth-bin quantisation error, splatted into a 64 x 48 BEV at 0.375 m. Private data: 87.75 drivable / 57.26 vehicle IoU; no ablation, no latency, no code. Shows the camera model entering only through a ray table.
idea: ray LUT for any camera model; covariance includes bin quantisation

title: WidthFormer: Toward Efficient Transformer-based BEV View Transformation (IROS 2024)
text: Height-max-pooled width features as keys and values of one decoder layer; depth bins enter as a reference positional encoding, not as a feature weight. nuScenes detection at 256 x 704: view transform 1.5 ms on a 3090 and 2.8 ms on Horizon Journey-5 vs 4.5 ms for LSS in its ablation. No segmentation; code licence not stated.
idea: speed reference for a learned lift

title: BEVFormer v2: Adapting Modern Image Backbones to Bird's-Eye-View Recognition via Perspective Supervision
text: Adds a perspective-space 3D detection head whose proposals feed the BEV head; the BEV lift stays BEVFormer's spatial cross-attention, no depth-weighted lift. Abstract page only, no numbers.

title: RadarPillars: Efficient Object Detection from 4D Radar Point Clouds (ITSC 2024)
text: VoD 4D radar: compensated radial velocity split into cos(azimuth) v_r and sin(azimuth) v_r (+3.8 mAP over PointPillars 39.5, the largest single step), PointNet pillars, PillarAttention (self-attention over occupied pillars only; core IS attention; +1.1 to +3.4 mAP in the ablation), 3-stage CNN of constant width 32. 1 frame entire-area mAP 46.0 vs 39.5; 5 frames 50.7. 0.27 M parameters, 1.99 GFLOPs, 86.6 Hz V100, 184.5 Hz RTX 3090. Text and Table III disagree on the attention gain; no code.
idea: ray direction inside the Doppler feature; narrow constant width

title: SMURF: Spatial Multi-Representation Fusion for 3D Object Detection with 4D Imaging Radar (T-IV 2024)
text: No attention. PointPillars branch plus two kernel-density branches whose kernel is a product over x, y, z and Doppler (bandwidths 1.5 / 2 m VoD), sparse 3D convs, concatenation, FPN neck. VoD val 5 scans mAP3D 50.97 (corridor 69.72); TJ4DRadSet test 32.99; KDE worth +2.93 / +3.02 mAP3D; 0.033 s per scan VoD (GPU not named). Hand-designed density feature that includes the Doppler axis; printed kernel has a sign typo; no code.
idea: density of neighbours in space and Doppler as a point feature

title: RadarGNN: Transformation Invariant Graph Neural Network for Radar-based Perception (CVPRW 2023)
text: kNN graph (k = 20) over 500 ms of RadarScenes points, edge features from relative position (translation invariant) or point-pair distance and velocity angles (rotation invariant), max-aggregation MPNN, no attention. mAP at IoU 0.3: no invariance 19.4, translation 56.5, translation + rotation 19.6; segmentation F1 68.1 / 77.1 / 76.5; beats PointNet++ F1 74.3. No latency. Code GPL-3.0.
idea: relative offsets yes; rotation invariance of the sensor frame no

title: RadarNeXt: Real-Time and Reliable 3D Object Detector Based On 4D mmWave Imaging Radar
text: No attention. Pillars (64 channels, 0.16 m), MobileOne re-parameterised depthwise backbone, one DCNv3 deformable conv level, PAN + FPN, CenterHead. VoD val 5 scans mAP 50.48 with 1.58 M parameters (dense 4.7 M backbone 48.9); TJ4DRadSet 32.30; 67.1 FPS on an RTX A4000, 28.4 FPS Jetson AGX Orin. DCNv3 placement swings mAP 46.96 to 50.48. Apache-2.0 repo.
idea: deformable conv follows position error; small conv-only radar BEV net

title: RadarDistill: Boosting Radar-based Object Detection Performance via Knowledge Distillation from LiDAR Features (CVPR 2024)
text: nuScenes radar-only test: 20.5 mAP / 43.7 NDS vs PillarNet 8.6 / 34.7, KPConvPillars 4.9 / 13.9, Radar-PointGNN 0.5 / 3.4. Pillars + sparse 2D convs + CenterHead; CMA densifies the radar BEV with deformable and ConvNeXt blocks (+2.0 NDS), lidar feature distillation (AFD +4.4 NDS, PFD +1.0) in training only. No attention; no latency; radar attributes not listed on the pages read.
idea: radar BEV densification; point nets rank far below pillar CNNs on nuScenes

title: Improved Multi-Scale Grid Rendering of Point Clouds for Radar Object Detection Networks (KPBEV / KPPillarsBEV, FUSION 2023)
text: No attention. nuScenes radar (x, y, compensated v_r, RCS, dt; 5 sweeps): offsets and point count per point, KPConv evaluated at non-empty cell centres, written to a 0.5 m x 64 channel map, rendered at 4 scales into a ResNet. Car AP4.0 PointPillars 38.31, KPBEV 41.21 at the same speed (87 FPS V100), multi-scale KPPillarsBEV 43.68 at 60 FPS. No code, no feature ablation.
idea: per-point state in a KPConv then rendered at cell centres with offset inputs

title: Improved Orientation Estimation and Detection with Hybrid Object Detection Networks for Automotive Radar
text: Abstract only: a point-based network (GNN or KPConv) before grid rendering and a conv backbone; nuScenes car mAP +19.7 % over the next radar-only submission, orientation +11.5 % relative. The submitted KPConvPillars is 4.9 mAP / 13.9 NDS on the 10-class test set (RadarDistill table). Predecessor of KPBEV; PDF not readable.
idea: point stage before the grid

title: DoppDrive: Doppler-Driven Temporal Aggregation for Improved Radar Object Detection (ICCV 2025)
text: Old sweep points are shifted radially by the dynamic Doppler times dt after ego-motion, and each point gets its own aggregation window (T0 - Tk <= D / (|v| g(theta)), D = 2 m) from the tangential smear that grows with the angle. SMURF on aiMotive vehicle AP 74.6 none / 81.7 standard / 89.1 DoppDrive; LRR-Sim 89.2 / 91.1 / 93.3. 2.0 ms on a V100. No nuScenes or VoD; no code licence.
idea: radial shift by v dt and angle-dependent window

title: SMIFormer: Learning Spatial Feature Representation for 3D Object Detection from 4D Imaging Radar via Multi-View Interactive Transformers (Sensors 2023)
text: ATTENTION core. Voxels projected to BEV, front and side planes, window attention within and across views. VoD val mAP entire area / corridor 48.77 / 71.13 vs VoxelNet base 46.48 / 68.36 (self-attention +0.16 / +1.35, cross-view +1.18 / +1.13); 61 ms with window 4, GPU not named. Baselines retrained by the authors (PointPillars 45.4 here vs 39.5 in RadarPillars). No code.

title: SpaRC: Sparse Radar-Camera Fusion for 3D Object Detection
text: ATTENTION core. Light Point Transformer over raw radar points (4 stages 32-256 channels, patch 64, space-filling-curve order), range-adaptive radar aggregation (+4.1 NDS / +5.9 mAP over the camera baseline with local attention), no BEV grid. nuScenes val R50 62.0 NDS / 54.5 mAP; test 67.1 NDS / 60.0 mAP; whole detector 32.9 FPS (R18) to 7.2 FPS (R101) on an RTX 3090 FP16, radar share not reported. Code announced, not released.
idea: range-dependent radar neighbourhood radius

title: IRGNN: Efficient Invariant Radar Graph Neural Network for Radar Point Cloud Object Detection
text: Abstract only: RadarGNN-style translation and rotation invariant graph with residual message passing and a virtual node, RadarScenes; no numbers, GPU or code on the page.
idea: virtual node as global context

title: MVFAN: Multi-View Feature Assisted Network for 4D Radar Object Detection
text: Digest from a search summary: anchor-free single stage, position map generation reweighting foreground and background points, a radar-feature-assisted backbone that uses Doppler and RCS, parallel cylindrical-projection and pillar branches; Astyx and VoD. RadarPillars lists it at 39.4 mAP (VoD entire area, 1 frame). The PDF is too large for the fetch tool; not read.

title: RPFA-Net: a 4D Radar Pillar Feature Attention Network for 3D Object Detection (ITSC 2021)
text: Digest from the abstract record: PointNet in the pillar encoder replaced by self-attention over the points of a pillar (ATTENTION core); Astyx HiRes 2019 only, +8.13 % 3D mAP and +5.52 % BEV mAP over its PointPillars baseline; code at adept-thu/RPFA-Net (not opened). The pillar-level attention idea reappears in RadarPillars.

title: Radar-PointGNN: Graph Based Object Recognition for Unstructured Radar Point-cloud Data (IEEE Radar Conference 2021)
text: Digest: kNN graph over radar points, convolution along edges; the first radar object recognition model on nuScenes. On the nuScenes test leaderboard it scores 0.5 mAP / 3.4 NDS (RadarDistill table, checked) - a graph point network without a grid stays far below pillar CNNs there. No arXiv id; TU Delft repository copy not read.

title: PolarStream: Streaming Object Detection and Segmentation with Polar Pillars (NeurIPS 2021)
text: Lidar polar pillar grid with range-stratified convolution and normalisation (individual kernels per range region) and learned feature undistortion (interpolation from polar to Cartesian pillar locations by two small nets). nuScenes val mAP: polar 48.2, + stratified 49.1, + undistortion 48.6, both 50.3; Cartesian pillars same head 50.6, so plain polar loses 2.4 mAP in detection and the two repairs recover 2.1; segmentation mIoU polar 73.2 vs Cartesian 72.5; fixes cost about 0.5 ms on a V100. Table 4 layout garbled in extraction. Lidar, dense; strata count not stated.
idea: per-range kernels and learned polar-to-Cartesian interpolation repair polar-grid distortion

title: PC-BEV: An Efficient Polar-Cartesian BEV Fusion Framework for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation (AAAI 2025)
text: Precomputed polar-to-Cartesian index remap between a polar and a Cartesian BEV branch (zero padding, concat then conv): remap 0.04 ms vs 6.8 / 8.0 ms for point-based fusion (2080 Ti), whole network 31 ms vs 39 ms (V100). nuScenes lidarseg val mIoU Cartesian 71.4, polar 75.0, point-based fusion 76.2, remap fusion 78.2; SemanticKITTI val 56.5 / 61.2 / 66.4. Interpolation type not stated; text and table disagree on the fusion gain. Lidar segmentation.
idea: fixed per-calibration polar<->Cartesian table costs 0.04 ms; both domains beat either alone

title: PolarNet: An Improved Grid Representation for Online LiDAR Point Clouds Semantic Segmentation (CVPR 2020)
text: Polar (azimuth x radius) BEV grid with ring convolution; SemanticKITTI val mIoU spherical / Cartesian BEV / polar BEV: ResNet-FCN 41.6 / 49.2 / 52.5, DRN-DL 43.4 / 46.7 / 51.2, ResNet-DL 41.6 / 50.4 / 53.6, SqueezeSeg 31.8 / 42.6 / 42.2 (polar loses on the weakest backbone). Test 54.3 mIoU at 0.062 s (GPU not named). Read-back to points by cell index, no interpolation. Lidar density argument; segmentation only.
idea: polar grid helps where point density falls with range

title: Deep Open Space Segmentation using Automotive Radar (ICMIM 2020)
text: RA / RAD radar spectra of a parking radar (SCORP; 3193 train / 720 eval frames), FCN / DeepLabV3+: polar in with Cartesian mask out (network learns the domain change, no dedicated layer) 77.2 to 78.2 mIoU for RA input; Cartesian in and out 78.1 to 80.8; polar in and out 81.1 to 82.6 (different label). Same domain wins in all rows; FCN-tiny 324 FPS on an RTX 2080 Ti. Small dataset, interpolation not named, the label domain changes between rows.
idea: do not make the CNN learn the polar-to-Cartesian geometry

title: KPRNet: Improving projection-based LiDAR semantic segmentation (ECCV 2020)
text: Range-image CNN features projected back to 3D points, then a KPConv layer replaces KNN voting: SemanticKITTI val mIoU KNN 57.7 (145 x 2049) / 61.7 (289 x 4097), KPConv 64.1 (+2.4 at the same input); test 63.1. No latency; radius and neighbour count not given. Lidar labels; argues against a hard nearest read-back.
idea: learned continuous-offset kernel for the last hop to irregular positions beats a fixed vote

title: CRN: Camera Radar Net for Accurate, Robust, Efficient 3D Perception (ICCV 2023)
text: Radar-assisted view transformation: radar points voxelised in camera frustum pillars give a sigmoid radar occupancy that multiplies the camera depth distribution before voxel pooling. nuScenes val NDS / mAP depth only 43.9 / 33.2, + radar occupancy 52.1 / 44.8, radar occupancy replacing depth 33.6 / 24.3. Multi-modal deformable attention fusion (6 layers) costs 21.0 ms dense or 4.96 ms with 4096 sparse queries (256 x 256 BEV, RTX 3090 FP16 batch 1); whole net 20.4 FPS (R50). Detection, frustum not polar.
idea: radar likelihood times camera depth probability; sigmoid occupancy; measured attention cost

title: PolarFormer: Multi-camera 3D Object Detection with Polar Transformers (AAAI 2023)
text: ATTENTION core. Polar BEV features from image columns; nuScenes val mAP / NDS Cartesian 37.8 / 45.4, polar features with Cartesian prediction 38.5 / 45.0, full polar 39.6 / 45.8; polar loss instead of Cartesian loss 31.5 / 38.2 (loss belongs in the output domain). No latency; conversion polar to Cartesian head not described.
idea: train through the output-domain loss

title: End-to-End Multi-View Fusion for 3D Object Detection in LiDAR Point Clouds (MVF / dynamic voxelization CoRL 2019)
text: Dynamic voxelization keeps every point and the point-to-voxel and voxel-to-point maps: no cap per voxel, no zero padding, no random drop; hard voxelization (VoxelNet / PointPillars) reserves 100 or more points per voxel and drops by random sampling. Same detector, only the voxelization changed (Waymo vehicle 3D AP 56.62 -> 59.29, BEV AP 75.57 -> 77.18; pedestrian 59.25 -> 60.83; KITTI car moderate 74.7 -> 77.86), latency 41.1 -> 41.1 ms vehicle, 36.1 -> 34.7 ms pedestrian. The fraction of points dropped by hard voxelization is not reported. Page read as ar5iv text (checked).
idea: lossless point-to-cell grouping by index and rank; pooled cell feature handed back to each point

title: BEV-MAE: Bird's Eye View Masked Autoencoders for Point Cloud Pre-training in Autonomous Driving Scenarios (AAAI 2024)
text: BEV-guided masking of whole BEV cells; decoder is one 3x3 conv with two linear heads: 20 points per masked cell as offsets from the cell centre (Chamfer) and the point density (Smooth-L1). Waymo 20 percent labels CenterPoint L2 mAP/APH: scratch 65.60/63.21, coordinates only 66.20/63.71, coordinates + density 66.70/64.25; nuScenes test 71.7 NDS / 67.0 mAP vs 70.2 / 65.5 for TransFusion-L. 38 h for 30 epochs on 8 P40; BEV masking 4.1 GB vs 12.6 GB for voxel masking. Lidar, masked prediction, not self-reconstruction; checked on the HTML page.
idea: K slots of offsets per BEV cell + a count/density head

title: R2LDM: An Efficient 4D Radar Super-Resolution Framework Leveraging Diffusion Model
text: Stage 1: a voxel feature encoder maps radar points to a latent grid; the decoder predicts an occupancy mask and an offset per voxel (P = (centre + offset) * mask) with mask BCE 0.9 + offset L1 0.1; only the average position of the points of a voxel is reconstructed. Stage 2: latent voxel diffusion to the lidar-like target (40.1 M parameters, 128 steps, 9 h + 21 h on an RTX 2080Ti, inference time not reported). VoD CD 0.64 vs 7.36 (R2DM), F-score 0.43 vs 0.08; registration recall 25.6 -> 57.3 percent. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: mask + offset per cell decoder; stage 1 alone as an auxiliary autoencoder

title: Diffusion-Based Point Cloud Super-Resolution for mmWave Radar Data (Radar-diffusion ICRA 2024)
text: Radar points of 5 frames aggregated by relative pose into a 256 x 256 BEV image (height as grey value); mean-reverting-SDE diffusion gives a denser lidar-like image. VoD: RadarHD CD 0.34 / MHD 0.24 -> 0.19 / 0.10; on the RadarHD data set it is worse in CD (0.44 -> 0.59). One RTX 4090 for 9 h; inference time not reported. The numbers set the scale (0.2-0.4 m) of radar-to-lidar point reconstruction, they do not test self-reconstruction. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: one-directional Chamfer / Hausdorff for how many real points are recovered

title: ALSO: Automotive Lidar Self-supervision by Occupancy estimation (CVPR 2023)
text: Pretext task: a 4-layer MLP (128 units) takes the latent of a support point and the offset of a query and outputs occupancy; queries in front of / behind a lidar return and on the sight line, BCE. nuScenes mIoU MinkUNet 0.1 / 1 / 10 / 100 percent labels 21.6 / 35.0 / 57.3 / 71.2 -> 26.2 / 37.4 / 59.0 / 71.8; KITTI moderate R40 SECOND 65.35 -> 68.07, PV-RCNN 70.57 -> 72.53; one 16 GB V100. Gain fades with labels; radar would need other labels. Checked (HTML up to character 100,000).
idea: continuous-offset query decoder as a training-only reconstruction head
licence: open source licence not named on the page

title: Convolutional Occupancy Networks (ECCV 2020)
text: Per-point PointNet features are average-pooled onto planes or a volume, a U-Net processes the grid, a small MLP decodes occupancy at any query by bi/trilinear interpolation. ShapeNet 3-plane 64^2 IoU 0.884 / Chamfer-L1 0.044 / F-score 0.942 vs global-latent ONet 0.761 / 0.087 / 0.785; rooms 64^3 volume IoU 0.849 vs 0.475; bilinear 0.805 vs nearest 0.766; volume 32^3 -> 64^3 0.782 -> 0.849. Runtime not on the page. Shows a mean-pooled grid decodes well when the per-point MLP runs before the pooling and the query is continuous. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: grid encode + continuous-query decode; regress attributes of the nearest detection as a probe
licence: not stated on the page (memory MIT; to check)

title: Deep Set Prediction Networks (DSPN NeurIPS 2019)
text: Set decoding by gradient descent on a learnable set so that its encoding matches the target latent; avoids the responsibility problem of MLP slots. MNIST auto-encoding Chamfer x1e-3 0.09 vs MLP 0.21 vs RNN 0.49; CLEVR AP95 85.7 vs 57.9 (evaluation bug noted by the authors); T = 10 steps cost about 75 percent more training time. States that Chamfer gives loss 0 for {a,a,b} vs {a,b,b} (blind to multiplicity) and that Hungarian is one-to-one at O(n^3). Checked on ar5iv.
idea: Chamfer cannot see duplicates: add a count term; exhaustive permutation min for K <= 4

title: Objects as Points (CenterNet)
text: Heat-map peak at stride 4 plus an L1 sub-cell offset head (weight 1, evaluated only at keypoints) that recovers the rounding error. COCO: 614 pairs of 860,001 objects share a centre cell at stride 4 (<0.1 percent cannot be predicted); with ground-truth heat-map, size and offset about 0.5 percent of objects are still missed (discretisation and Gaussian rendering). The only collision statistic found; it does not transfer to radar returns in a 0.5 m cell, which has to be measured. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: cell + offset code as the decodable position representation

title: PointRNN: Point Recurrent Neural Network for Moving Point Cloud Processing
text: State = point coordinates + a per-point state tensor; old and new points are paired by kNN or ball query on coordinates, the update concatenates the own feature, the neighbour state and the displacement, shared FC + max pool; GRU / LSTM variants. Future point prediction CD / EMD: nuScenes 0.0619 / 0.3750, Argoverse 0.2789 / 0.8964; Moving MNIST 2 digits PointLSTM 5.18 / 4.21 (ball query beats kNN); 49.6 GFLOPs vs 345 GFLOPs for a voxel ConvLSTM. Lidar-scale clouds, prediction task, no detection or map result. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: history kept as aligned points with a state; raster built once

title: RV-FuseNet: Range View Based Fusion of Time-Series LiDAR Data for Joint 3D Object Detection and Motion Forecasting
text: Past sweeps are ego-aligned and merged in the range view; early (warp all to the latest view) vs late vs incremental (fuse sweep by sweep, small viewpoint steps). nuScenes AP at 0.7 / L2 at 3 s: 57.9 / 135 cm, 58.8 / 127 cm, 59.9 / 120 cm. States that information loss and gaps grow with ego and actor speed. No cost comparison. Evidence that many small alignment steps beat one big one; the winning variant passes features, not points. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: sweep-by-sweep recurrent update with small steps

title: Semantic-Supervised Spatial-Temporal Fusion for LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection (ST-Fusion)
text: CenterPoint on nuScenes val mAP / NDS: single frame 57.28 / 65.58, data fusion (points concatenated, time lag attribute) 58.86 / 66.43, feature fusion 59.79 / 67.48, ST-Fusion 60.48 / 68.32. Data fusion NDS by number of frames: 65.58 / 66.19 / 66.43 / 66.07 for k = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, so it saturates at 4. Authors blame object motion; no ego or Doppler correction described; no latency. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: point accumulation alone saturates; number of sweeps has an optimum

title: ALICE-LRI: A General Method for Lossless Range Image Generation for Spinning LiDAR Sensors without Calibration Metadata
text: Infers the beam layout, angular distribution and per-beam corrections from the cloud itself so that every point has its own range-image pixel; zero points lost on all of KITTI and DurLAR (abstract page only; no equations, no code). Conventional projection is many-to-one (digest from a search summary). Principle: invertible iff injective plus a stored residual.
idea: invertibility of a sensor-grid image = injective cell assignment + stored residual

title: On the Limitations of Representing Functions on Sets
text: Continuous sum-decomposition rho(sum phi(x)) of permutation-invariant functions on sets of at most M scalars works through R^M (Thm 4.4) and not through R^N with N < M in general (Thm 4.1); similar for max-pooling. Scalars only; toy median experiment shows the useful latent size grows about linearly with M but below M. Argument for K explicit slots instead of one pooled vector per cell. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: pooled cell vector must be as wide as the set it must hold

title: VoxelNet: End-to-End Learning for Point Cloud Based 3D Object Detection
text: Voxels with more than T points are randomly sub-sampled (T = 35 car, 45 pedestrian / cyclist); at most K non-empty voxels are kept; more than 90 percent of voxels are empty; voxel coordinates are hash keys so a point is inserted in O(1) and dropped if its voxel is full (buffers built in one pass). 225 ms on a TitanX of which 170 ms in the 3D middle convs. The origin of the capped per-cell list. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: capped per-cell list as the lossy baseline
extract: skip: row only (facts used in the MVF note)

title: Occupancy-MAE: Self-supervised Pre-training Large-scale LiDAR Point Clouds with Masked Occupancy Autoencoders (first posted as Voxel-MAE)
text: Range-aware random masking of occupied voxels (90 / 70 / 50 percent for 0-30 / 30-50 / over 50 m); the decoder reconstructs only the binary occupancy of each voxel, focal loss, no coordinates; KITTI car 3D moderate 72.55 -> 72.87, cyclist 52.08 -> 54.84; Waymo vehicle L1 AP SECOND 72.27 -> 73.68 with all data; nuScenes 3-frame +1.8 mAP / +1.4 NDS (CenterPoint), single frame +0.5 mAP; about half of the car labels match full-data scratch. No cost figures. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: range-dependent masking ratio

title: GD-MAE: Generative Decoder for MAE Pre-training on LiDAR Point Clouds (CVPR 2023)
text: Reconstruction target: the points of each masked token (at most 64) in token-local coordinates, L2 Chamfer; the generative decoder takes 3.2 ms vs 27.1 ms for a transformer decoder baseline. Waymo mAPH L2 with / without pre-training: 5 percent labels 59.97 -> 63.86, 20 percent 65.35 -> 67.14, 100 percent 67.34 -> 67.64; ONCE mAP 62.62 -> 64.92. No GPU hours. Checked on the HTML page.
idea: local-coordinate point targets per token

title: UniPAD: A Universal Pre-training Paradigm for Autonomous Driving (CVPR 2024)
text: Masked lidar / multi-view inputs lifted to a voxel volume, SDF rendering of depth and RGB along sampled rays, weighted L1 (both weights 10). nuScenes val NDS UVTR-L 67.7 -> 70.6, UVTR-C 45.0 -> 47.4, UVTR-M 70.2 -> 73.2; SpUNet 73.3 -> 79.4 mIoU. Depth-aware ray sampling 32.9 NDS at 1x memory vs 32.5 random and 31.9 dilated. No code link on the page. Rendering is a camera-side idea; checked on the HTML page.
idea: rendering loss for a volume

title: MAELi: Masked Autoencoder for Large-Scale LiDAR Point Clouds (WACV 2024)
text: Abstract page only: masking tied to the sensor's spherical projection and a reconstruction that separates empty space from occluded space (the sensor-blind-spot idea); no numbers or loss form on the page read. Relevant to radar because most of a radar scene is not observed.
idea: separate empty from unobserved space in the reconstruction loss

title: Masked Autoencoder for Self-Supervised Pre-training on Lidar Point Clouds (Voxel-MAE Hess et al.)
text: Digest from a search summary: reconstructs masked voxels and classifies empty vs non-empty; nuScenes +1.75 mAP / +1.05 NDS; 40 percent of the labels with pre-training beat a randomly initialised model. Not opened.

title: VoxelContext-Net: An Octree based Framework for Point Cloud Compression
text: Octree occupancy symbols of non-leaf nodes are coded losslessly with a context network; the distortion comes only from the octree depth (quantisation) and a coordinate refinement module predicts offsets at the decoder. SemanticKITTI saves 31.15 percent bitrate vs G-PCC (OctSqueeze 2.13 percent), 55.51 dB at 0.36 bpp vs 54.35 dB at 0.52 bpp; decoding 52-90 ms on a 2080Ti, 2.15 M parameters. Compression coder, not a feature encoder. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: occupancy code + decoder-side offset refinement

title: OctSqueeze: Octree-Structured Entropy Model for LiDAR Compression (CVPR 2020)
text: Octree with a learned entropy model of the occupancy byte given the ancestors; loss only from the leaf depth (12-16 levels). KITTI example 43.67 PSNR at 1.52 vs Draco 39.09 at 2.04; downstream NorthAmerica detection AP 86.17 at 3.39 vs 85.27 at 5.00 (Draco); encode 49.6-106 ms, decode 166-902 ms on a GTX 1080. Examples are hand-picked. Checked on the supplement via ar5iv.

title: Sparse Tensor-based Multiscale Representation for Point Cloud Geometry Compression (SparsePCGC)
text: Multiscale sparse tensors, per-scale occupancy probability on the most probable occupied voxels (SOPA, SLNE); claims state of the art in lossless and lossy mode on 8iVFB / Owlii / MUVB / KITTI / Ford; no bpp numbers or code link on the abstract page.

title: 4D Spatio-Temporal ConvNets: Minkowski Convolutional Neural Networks
text: Sparse tensor = coordinate matrix C + feature matrix F (COO); quantisation (Alg. 1) sorts and reduces by key and keeps ONE representative index per voxel, so the other points of the voxel are dropped (labels in conflict set to ignore). Generalised sparse convolution on arbitrary output coordinates; 4D net adds under 6.4 percent parameters. Hash-based sparse tensors are lossless only if the quantised coordinates are unique. Checked on ar5iv.
idea: sparse tensor with unique coordinates; duplicates lost at quantisation

title: Voxel Set Transformer: A Set-to-Set Approach to 3D Object Detection from Point Clouds (VoxSeT CVPR 2022)
text: Abstract page: self-attention inside each voxel through two cross-attentions with a few learned latent codes, so voxels of arbitrary size are handled in parallel at linear cost; competitive on KITTI and Waymo; a search summary states that it avoids the stochastic point dropout of equal-sized grouping (digest). No latency on the page. Per-cell set encoder without a cap.
idea: per-cell latent-code attention for variable-size cells

title: FoldingNet: Point Cloud Auto-Encoder via Deep Grid Deformation
text: Decoder warps a fixed 2025-point (45 x 45) grid concatenated with a 512-d code through two 3-layer MLPs to the point cloud (about 1.05 M parameters, 7 percent of a fully connected decoder); extended Chamfer (max of the two directions). ModelNet40 Chamfer test loss 0.0296 (2 folds) / 0.0290 (3 folds). Global-code decoder, not cell-aligned. Checked on ar5iv.
code: licence at merl.com (terms not on the page)

title: Learning Representations and Generative Models for 3D Point Clouds (Achlioptas et al.)
text: Chamfer vs EMD as autoencoder training loss: the EMD-trained AE gives better generative results and CD is cheaper; CD 'fails to distinguish' samples that overpopulate a region. Chair AE: MMD-CD 0.0004 / 0.0012 (train / test) with the CD-trained AE, MMD-EMD 0.068 / 0.075; EMD-trained 0.0005 / 0.0013 and 0.042 / 0.052; 2048 points, bottleneck 128. Checked on ar5iv.

title: High Resolution Point Clouds from mmWave Radar (RadarHD ICRA 2023)
text: 64 x 256 polar heat-map of 40 stacked frames, asymmetric U-Net to a 512 x 256 lidar-style image, BCE + Dice, threshold to points. Median Chamfer 0.36 m / MHD 0.24 m in the training environment (3.5x and 2.7x better than CFAR), 0.8 / 0.75 m and 1.03 / 0.94 m in two unseen environments. No code URL on the page. Checked on ar5iv and the abstract page.

title: UniFusion: Unified Multi-view Fusion Transformer for Spatial-Temporal Representation in Bird's-Eye-View
text: Abstract page only: spatial and temporal fusion in one formulation with learnable temporal weights; claims less information loss than warping fixed-size BEV memories and state of the art map segmentation on nuScenes; no numbers or code on the page. The 'virtual views' idea named in a search summary was not on the page.

title: Hidden Gems: 4D Radar Scene Flow Learning Using Cross-Modal Supervision (CMFlow CVPR 2023)
text: Digest from a search summary: flow split into a rigid ego-motion part (differentiable weighted Kabsch from the first flow estimate) and a residual; static background flow supervised from the radar ego-motion, foreground from tracked boxes; co-located lidar / camera / GPS-INS only as training supervision. Used for motion segmentation and ego-motion. Not opened.
idea: per-point motion = ego part + residual

title: Dual-Weight Particle Filter for Radar-Based Dynamic Bayesian Grid Maps
text: Each particle has a position, a velocity and two weights (position, velocity); the radial velocity is projected into x-y and rewards particles whose velocity matches a nearby measurement. Simulated roads (MATLAB toolbox, 200 m x 25 m at 0.5 m, 10,000 particles): simple road dv 0.39 m/s, dx 0.53 m, tracked 91 percent; highway tracked 63 percent vs 34 / 40 percent. No runtime, no real data, no ego-motion description on the page. Particles move as points, so there is no grid resampling. Checked on ar5iv.

title: Masked-reconstruction self-supervised pre-training on radar point clouds (Takai et al. Kanazawa University JSAE 2026)
text: Digest from a search summary (abstract behind a login): self-supervised pre-training by masked reconstruction on radar point clouds, tested on object detection; no numbers, no data set named. The only radar masked-reconstruction work found; no arXiv version.

title: BEV-SAN: Accurate BEV 3D Object Detection via Slice Attention Networks (CVPR 2023)
text: One BEV feature per height slice (global [-6 4] [-5 3] [-4 2] m, local slices from a LiDAR height histogram whose peaks are near -2 and 0) merged by SE attention and a two-way transformer. nuScenes val ResNet-50 NDS 0.366 vs BEVDepth 0.336 (no CBGS); slices ablation baseline 0.330, global 0.343, local 0.351, both 0.366; LiDAR-guided 0.366 vs even 0.359; 15.4 vs 24.3 FPS. Detection only, motivation is class heights not thin surfaces, no code.
idea: choose the heights of the pull lift from a LiDAR height histogram

title: DualPathOcc: Dual-Resolution BEV Encoder for 3D Occupancy Prediction (2026)
text: Controlled depth-target ablation on Occ3D-nuScenes val mIoU (no spatial enhancer): one-hot LiDAR depth 35.96, no depth loss 36.92, Gaussian-softened target (sigma 1.5 bins) 36.94; final model 37.37 with no depth loss.
