A one-hot first-surface target costs about 1 mIoU in a densely supervised BEV task. Occupancy not segmentation, one table, no code.
idea: Gaussian along the depth axis for the depth target

title: Exploring Object-Centric Temporal Modeling for Efficient Multi-View 3D Object Detection (StreamPETR, ICCV 2023)
text: FIFO memory of 4 frames x 256 top object queries moved by the relative ego transform; motion-aware LayerNorm from [ego transform velocity dt]. nuScenes val R50: 0.432 mAP / 0.540 NDS at 27.1 FPS vs SOLOFusion 0.427 / 0.534 at 11.4 FPS; memory 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 frames NDS 0.372 / 0.501 / 0.505 / 0.505 (mAVE 0.885 / 0.324 / 0.314 / 0.316); explicit motion compensation alone did not help (NDS 0.481) while implicit ego-pose encoding gave +2.0 mAP. Object queries not a dense grid.
idea: state is a list of originals moved by exact transforms; dt/velocity/ego as a conditioning vector

title: Sparse4D v2: Recurrent Temporal Fusion with Sparse Model
text: Recurrent propagation of sparse instances: only the anchor (3D box plus velocity) is projected (position + velocity x dt, then ego rotation and translation) while the instance feature is copied unchanged. RTX 3090 R50: v1 multi-frame sampling 21.5 / 12.6 / 9.0 / 6.1 FPS for T = 1 / 3 / 5 / 9, v2 flat 19.4 FPS and 432 MB; temporal vs none NDS 0.414 to 0.539. No matched NDS of recurrent vs window.
idea: move the coordinates and copy the content; O(1) history cost

title: OnlineBEV: Recurrent Temporal Fusion in Bird's Eye View Representations for Multi-Camera 3D Perception
text: One BEV memory; motion-guided deformable warping attention (offsets from the difference of current and historical queries) and a temporal consistency loss (same head on current and aligned history, squared L2, gradient stopped on the current side). nuScenes val R50 44.4 mAP / 54.5 NDS / 0.244 mAVE vs SOLOFusion 17 frames 42.7 / 53.4 / 0.252; motion-guided fusion +1.0 NDS (mAVE 0.296 to 0.287), HTC-loss +0.5 NDS; 12.6 vs 13.8 FPS. No code.
idea: label-free alignment loss: aligned past must give the same heatmap as the present

title: Self-Supervised Pillar Motion Learning for Autonomous Driving (SPML, CVPR 2021)
text: Pillar motion without flow labels: weighted symmetric chamfer between the moved point cloud and the next sweep (static pillars down-weighted), cross-sensor L1 to camera object-motion flow (weight 0.01), smoothness; 0.25 m pillars 64 m square, 20 ms per sweep. nuScenes motion error static / slow / fast: self-supervised 0.162 / 0.697 / 3.550, fine-tuned 0.0245 / 0.229 / 0.778, supervised MotionNet 0.0239 / 0.247 / 1.011. Label-free is not a replacement for labels but a better start on fast objects.
idea: forward-warp and compare with the next observation plus a static-mask weight

title: ContrastMotion: Self-supervised Scene Motion Learning for Large-Scale LiDAR Point Clouds (IJCAI 2023)
text: Pillar features of t and t+1 associated by a softmax over feature distance in a local patch; trained by contrast on an augmented copy with a known rigid transform (soft positives 0.6 exact, 0.1 neighbours). nuScenes mean error static / slow / fast: 0.083 / 0.452 / 3.527 vs SPML 0.162 / 0.697 / 3.550 vs zero motion 0.000 / 0.611 / 8.652. No supervised comparison on the page, no code.
idea: synthetic known-transform correspondence as free label; local correlation association

title: PowerBEV: A Powerful Yet Lightweight Framework for Instance Prediction in Bird's-Eye View (IJCAI 2023)
text: Segmentation plus centripetal backward flow (vector from a foreground pixel at t to its instance centre at t-1, smooth L1) from a 2D-conv multi-scale U-Net that predicts all future frames in parallel; warping association with backward flow beats Hungarian with forward flow (VPQ 39.2 vs 38.3 short, 33.5 vs 31.9 long at 2 s). nuScenes IoU / VPQ 62.5 / 55.5 short and 39.3 / 33.8 long vs FIERY 59.4 / 50.2 and 36.7 / 29.9; 39.3 M vs 8.4 M parameters, 92.6 vs 206.8 GFLOPs. No no-flow ablation.
idea: backward flow target that a grid_sample pull can use

title: SelfOccFlow: self-supervised 3D occupancy flow without annotations or external flow supervision (2026)
text: Flow pseudo-labels from cosine similarity of BEV dynamic features of t and t+-1 inside a 35 x 35 window (arg-max displacement, L1 weight 5.0, forward-backward consistency weight); static / dynamic SDFs; no pretrained optical-flow net. nuScenes occupancy flow RayIoU / mAVE 41.39 / 1.31 vs OccNet (3D-supervised) 39.66 / 1.61 and LetOccFlow-L 40.48 / 1.45; 32.4 M parameters, 3.78 FPS on a V100. Without the similarity loss the flow is not learned; preprint, no code.
idea: label-free flow by local feature correlation with a forward-backward mask

title: Let Occ Flow: Self-Supervised 3D Occupancy Flow Prediction (CoRL 2024)
text: TPV occupancy with an SDF and a 3D flow field, rendered; dynamic flow = optical flow minus the static flow implied by rendered depth; pretrained 2D optical flow and GroundedSAM as cues. nuScenes RayIoU / mAVE camera-only 30.12 / 1.42, camera + LiDAR 40.48 / 1.45 vs OccNet 39.66 / 1.61; flow supervision lowers foreground EPE 9.66 to 7.51 on KITTI-MOT; 253 M parameters.
idea: observed flow minus the flow the static scene would give

title: Self-Supervised Scene Flow Estimation with 4-D Automotive Radar (RaFlow, RA-L 2022)
text: Per-point radar scene flow: set-conv encoder, cost volume, flow decoder, static refinement; losses radial displacement (flow projected on the line of sight equals Doppler x dt), soft Chamfer, smoothness; ego motion by Kabsch with a static set chosen by the radial residual (<= 15 %). In-house 4D radar 43.6 km: EPE 0.570 m, radial error 0.240 m, motion segmentation accuracy 81.9 %; removing Doppler hurts most. One test sequence, no runtime.
idea: Doppler as the radial label of the flow; static set from the radial residual
code: https://github.com/Toytiny/RaFlow (named in the paper; not verified)

title: Full-Velocity Radar Returns by Radar-Camera Fusion (ICCV 2021)
text: Closed-form per-point full velocity from the radial Doppler plus the optical flow at the point's pixel (constant velocity over dt; a 3 x 3 solve per point) and a learned radar-pixel association net (U-Net R2P). nuScenes point-wise velocity error 0.433 m/s with R2P vs 0.577 raw projection vs 1.599 radial-only; tangential 0.322 vs 1.536; objects 0.451 vs CenterFusion 0.826; RAFT 0.447 s, R2P 2.58 ms, solve 0.249 ms. No code found.
idea: second observation of the same point gives the missing tangential component by a linear solve

title: CR3DT: Camera-RADAR Fusion for 3D Detection and Tracking
text: Five radar sweeps pillar-averaged into a 128 x 128 BEV grid (0.8 m, 18 features) concatenated with the lifted camera BEV; nuScenes val mAVE 0.47 vs 0.86 m/s for camera-only BEVDet R50 (minus 45.3 %), mAP 35.1 vs 29.8, NDS 45.6 vs 37.9; tracker uses the detector velocity (AMOTA 31.2 to 38.1). No radar-off ablation of the velocity.
idea: accumulate sweeps and pillar-average the compensated velocity: the baseline arm

title: GeoBEV: Learning Geometric BEV Representation for Multi-view 3D Object Detection (AAAI 2025)
text: Abstract only: Radial-Cartesian BEV sampling for dense high-resolution BEV, an In-Box depth label (full object volume instead of the LiDAR surface) and a centroid-aware inner loss; 66.2 NDS on nuScenes test. Mechanism and ablations not read.
idea: depth label of the volume instead of the first surface

title: SMURF: Self-Teaching Multi-Frame Unsupervised RAFT with Full-Image Warping (CVPR 2021)
text: Abstract only: RAFT trained without labels with a sequence-aware self-supervision loss and handling of out-of-frame motion; 36 to 40 percent better than the best earlier unsupervised method (UFlow) and better than some supervised nets (PWC-Net FlowNet2). Optical flow on images, no BEV; census / photometric details not read.
idea: all-pairs correlation volume trained by warping and multi-frame self-teaching

title: Cam4DOcc: Benchmark for Camera-Only 4D Occupancy Forecasting in Autonomous Driving Applications (CVPR 2024)
text: Abstract only: nuScenes / Lyft based benchmark with sequential occupancy of movable and static objects plus 3D backward centripetal flow; four baseline families (static world, voxelised point-cloud prediction, 2D-3D instance prediction, own end-to-end network). Metrics not read.
idea: backward centripetal flow in 3D as supervision

title: Softmax Splatting for Video Frame Interpolation (Niklaus & Liu CVPR 2020)
text: Forward warp with four variants read on ar5iv: summation (bilinear kernel, overlaps add), average (divided by splatted ones), linear (weights Z) and softmax (weights exp(Z), normalised, shift-invariant in Z); only softmax separates a car from the background it passes. CUDA layer softsplat(tenIn tenFlow tenMetric strMode) with alpha -20 in the example. PSNR ablation not read. Dense frames: our version adds a mass channel for unknown cells and uses the hypothesis probability as importance.
idea: hypothesis probability times importance as softmax weight; mass as known/unknown

title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow (Teed & Deng ECCV 2020)
text: Verified id and claims: all-pairs correlation volume pooled to a multi-scale pyramid and a weight-tied GRU that looks up the volume around the current flow, starting from zero, at ONE resolution (not coarse-to-fine). KITTI F1-all 5.10 vs 6.10; Sintel final EPE 2.855 vs 4.098; about 10 fps 1088x436 on a 1080Ti. Full volume (HW)^2 is too big for BEV; local window versions exist (ALOcc). One flow per pixel, no hypotheses.
idea: weight-tied refinement with sequence loss; zero-init flow

title: PWC-Net: CNNs for Optical Flow Using Pyramid Warping and Cost Volume (CVPR 2018)
text: Verified: Sun Yang Liu Kautz; CVPR 2018 camera-ready; pyramid features, warp of the second frame by the current flow, local cost volume, CNN estimator per level; 17x smaller than FlowNet2; about 35 fps on 1024x436 Sintel frames. Search range 4 and 8.75 M parameters from memory (ar5iv page empty). Warp then correlate keeps the search window to the residual motion.
idea: velocity pyramid: coarse all hypotheses then residual hypotheses

title: Unsupervised Learning of Depth and Ego-Motion from Video (SfMLearner CVPR 2017)
text: Section 3.4 Overcoming the gradient locality: the gradients are mainly derived from the pixel intensity difference between I(p_t) and the four neighbors of I(p_s); remedy explicit multi-scale and smoothness loss. This (and Monodepth2 Sec 3.2) is where the gradient-locality statement lives, not in Monodepth 1609.03677.
idea: multi-scale pooled loss on the splat output

title: Unsupervised Monocular Depth Estimation with Left-Right Consistency (Monodepth CVPR 2017)
text: Verified id and venue (Godard Mac Aodha Brostow CVPR 2017 oral). The text says the bilinear sampler is locally fully differentiable (Sec 3.3) and uses four output scales for more stable convergence (Sec 4.1); the words locality and local minima do not occur. The gradient-locality statement is in SfMLearner 1704.07813 and Monodepth2 1806.01260.
code: no link on the arXiv page

title: Digging Into Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation (Monodepth2 ICCV 2019)
text: Sec 3.2 Multi-scale Estimation contains the clause Due to the gradient locality of the bilinear sampler and says existing models use multi-scale prediction to prevent the training objective getting stuck in local minima; its own remedy is to upsample the low-resolution maps to the input resolution and compute the error there (against holes in low-texture regions and texture-copy). Text read on ar5iv.
idea: all scales evaluated at full resolution

title: Spatial Transformer Networks (Jaderberg et al. NIPS 2015)
text: Verified id and authors (Jaderberg Simonyan Zisserman Kavukcuoglu); v1 2015-06-05 v3 2016-02-04; a learnable differentiable module that spatially transforms feature maps conditioned on the feature map; arXiv page lists no venue (NIPS 2015 from memory). Backward sampling (grid_sample) ancestor of our pull arm; the forward splat is the transpose.

title: A Random Finite Set Approach for Dynamic Occupancy Grid Maps with Real-Time Application (Nuss et al. IJRR 2018)
text: Verified; the title ends with 'with Real-Time Application' (arXiv v1 2016-05-09 v2 2016-09-10; IJRR 37(8) 841-866 from a search result). PHD/MIB particle filter: particle = position + velocity + weight; constant-velocity prediction with noise; per-cell update; resampling to constant count; birth from measurement. Laser and radar fused. How Doppler enters, grid size and runtime not read (html cut at 100000 of 175000 characters).
idea: particle=(cell hypothesis weight); birth from measurement = learned hypotheses

title: Radar-based Dynamic Occupancy Grid Mapping and Object Detection (Diehl et al. 2020)
text: Radar-only particle DOGM (50 m grid 0.2 m cells at most 50 particles per cell): static particles are sampled by a radar pre-classification (direction SNR radial velocity ego motion) not by the radial velocity alone because an orthogonal mover has zero radial velocity. Moving vehicle velocity error 0.138 m/s radar vs 1.350 m/s lidar (one track static ego Berlin data). No likelihood formula no runtime.
idea: Doppler aperture: no radial velocity is not static; hypotheses on the Doppler ray

title: Dynamic Occupancy Grid Prediction for Urban Autonomous Driving: A Deep Learning Approach with Fully Automatic Labeling (Hoermann et al.)
text: A Bayesian-filter DOGMa (occupancy and per-cell velocity) is the input of a CNN that predicts the future; single time step input; automatic labels from past and future estimates; pixel-wise balancing for static vs dynamic cells; compared with Monte Carlo simulation. Abstract only (PDF unreadable); no numbers; laser; the filter is outside the network.
idea: automatic dynamic/static labels by tracking forward and backward

title: Object Detection on Dynamic Occupancy Grid Maps Using Deep Learning and Automatic Label Generation (Hoermann et al.)
text: Single-stage CNN from one DOGMa to object hypotheses (shape position orientation existence); offline forward/backward tracking labels; AP 75.9 percent (abstract). Laser DOGMa no radar.

title: Deep Object Tracking on Dynamic Occupancy Grid Maps Using RNNs (Engel Hoermann Henzler Dietmayer)
text: CNN plus recurrent net on a time series of DOGMas for static/dynamic separation and object tracking; AUC 0.946 for dynamic/static segmentation (abstract); laser scanners; auto labels.

title: Dynamic Occupancy Grid Mapping with Recurrent Neural Networks (Schreiber et al. ICRA 2021)
text: Learned DOGMa: lidar measurement grid (0.15 m 1001x1001) into a U-Net with ConvLSTM at four levels; outputs occupancy and east/north velocity; ego motion by input placement and recurrent state shifting at the coarsest cell size. Argoverse vs the particle DOGMa of Nuss: cell mIoU 0.8892 vs 0.6247; dynamic-cell EPE 0.1059 vs 0.1998 m; object velocity MAE 0.5173 vs 0.5264 m/s; 53 ms on a GTX 1080 Ti. Lidar only one velocity per cell no radar no hypotheses.
idea: evaluation protocol vs a classical DOGMa; velocity loss only on occupied cells

title: A Multi-Task Recurrent Neural Network for End-to-End Dynamic Occupancy Grid Mapping (Schreiber et al. IV 2022)
text: Same group: raw lidar BEV with height channels into one recurrent net that outputs occupancy velocity semantics and drivable area; learned inverse sensor model better on shapes and freespace than a geometric one; faster and more accurate semantics than the measurement-grid variant (abstract only no numbers).

title: Deep Learning-Driven State Correction: A Hybrid Architecture for Radar-Based Dynamic Occupancy Grid Mapping (Ronecker et al. IV 2024)
text: Abstract only: a particle-filter radar DOGM is poor at static/dynamic separation; a network (framed as semantic segmentation) corrects the static/dynamic state; heuristic fusion of filter and network for safety; evaluated on nuScenes for dynamic object detection and grid quality; no numbers read; body not readable.
idea: filter first then repair net on nuScenes radar

title: CRT-Fusion: Camera Radar Temporal Fusion Using Motion Information for 3D Object Detection (NeurIPS 2024)
text: Motion Feature Estimator (pixel-wise velocity plus BEV segmentation) and Motion Guided Temporal Fusion that aligns BEV features recurrently; +1.7 NDS and +1.4 mAP over the previous best radar-camera method (abstract); rest from our code note and plan 7.2: R50 57.2 NDS vs CRN 56.0 and the released velocity shift writes into a copy. Radar only as input channels; one velocity per cell; no isolated ablation of the shift.
idea: supervised per-cell velocity + velocity-guided warp as the baseline to beat

title: Unleashing HyDRa: Hybrid Fusion Depth Consistency and Radar for Unified 3D Perception (ICRA 2025)
text: Camera-radar fusion in perspective view (height association transformer for depth) and BEV (radar-weighted depth consistency). nuScenes val R50 NDS 58.5 mAP 49.4 mAVE 0.227; R101 61.7 / 53.6 / 0.231; test V2-99 64.2 NDS 58.4 AMOTA; Occ3D +3.7 mIoU. Eight history frames; CenterPoint-style head; the summary shows no Doppler channel handling and no velocity branch. Code announced as coming soon.

title: RCBEVDet: Radar-camera Fusion in Bird's Eye View for 3D Object Detection (CVPR 2024)
text: Val R50: mAVE BEVDet 0.909 BEVDepth 0.428 SOLOFusion 0.252 StreamPETR 0.295 CRN 0.344 RCBEVDet 0.220 (NDS 56.8 mAP 45.3 21.3 FPS RTX 3090 FP16). Test V2-99 mAVE 0.259 while camera-only SparseBEV 0.246 and StreamPETR 0.243 are lower. Doppler speed only as a point feature; velocity from stacked ego-aligned BEV history; text percentages disagree with its table. Radar does not clearly beat history on mAVE.
licence: academic only; code behind an application form

title: ALOcc: Adaptive Lifting-based 3D Semantic Occupancy and Cost Volume-based Flow Prediction (ICCV 2025)
text: BEV cost volume for occupancy flow: previous BEV feature warped to the current frame then cosine similarity at predefined offsets concatenated to the current BEV feature; flow as classification over bins plus expectation (L2 + cosine + cross-entropy); single pass. OpenOcc flow variant mAVE 0.537 (2D) / 0.556 (3D) Occ score 42.1 / 43.0; RTX 4090 30.5 FPS (2D-mini) to 6.0 FPS (3D). Camera only no Doppler; offsets fixed around zero.
idea: expected value over velocity bins vs our mixture splat

title: Spatiotemporal Decoupling for Efficient Vision-Based Occupancy Forecasting (EfficientOCF)
text: Abstract only: BEV occupancy plus height instead of a 3D grid and instances linked across frames by predicted backward centripetal flow; 82.33 ms on one GPU; code promised.

title: PillarFlow: End-to-end Birds-eye-view Flow Estimation for Autonomous Driving (Lee et al. IROS 2020)
text: Abstract only: lidar point cloud pairs into a 2-D BEV flow grid of cell dynamic states by a pillar network; improves tracking of dynamic and static objects; no numbers on the page; no code.

title: Scalable Scene Flow from Point Clouds in the Real World (FastFlow3D Jund et al. 2021)
text: Abstract only: large scene-flow dataset from tracked 3D objects (about 1000x more annotated frames) and FastFlow3D real-time on the full point cloud; downsampling heuristics hurt; ego-motion-aware metrics broken down by object type. Lidar; pillar/BEV grid details not read.
idea: ego-motion-aware metrics per object type

title: Occupancy Flow Fields for Motion Forecasting in Autonomous Driving (Mahjourian et al. RA-L 2022)
text: Abstract via search result: a grid over space and time with occupancy probability and a 2-D flow vector per cell; a flow trace loss keeps occupancy and flow consistent; INTERACTION and an in-house set. Mechanism and numbers not read.
idea: flow-trace consistency loss between occupancy and flow

title: Learning in an Uncertain World: Representing Ambiguity Through Multiple Hypotheses (Rupprecht et al. ICCV 2017)
text: Multiple hypothesis prediction with a meta loss: only the hypothesis whose Voronoi cell holds the label gets the loss; relaxed with eps 0.05 to the others plus about 1 percent hypothesis dropout against starved hypotheses; no score network; oracle numbers: LSP PCP 59.7 (1) to 62.8 (10 hypotheses); VOC2012 segmentation 70.3 vs 69.1 for MCL; NTU future min MSE 960.6 to 728.5. Best-of-M metrics only.
idea: eps-relaxed weights and hypothesis dropout as guards against dead hypotheses

title: Stochastic Multiple Choice Learning for Training Diverse Deep Ensembles (Lee et al. 2016)
text: Abstract only: SGD that minimises loss against an oracle over an ensemble of networks; architecture and loss independent; lower oracle error than earlier methods. The deep version of MCL (Guzman-Rivera et al. 2012 not looked up).

title: Differentiable Particle Filters: End-to-End Learning with Algorithmic Priors (Jonschkowski et al. RSS 2018)
text: Particle filter as a differentiable computation with learnable motion and measurement models trained end to end; about 80 percent error reduction and better policy generalisation than LSTMs on simulated and KITTI visual-odometry tasks (abstract). Method section not read; single-object localisation not a grid.

title: Self-Supervised Velocity Estimation for Automotive Radar Object Detection Networks (Niederlohner et al. IV 2022)
text: Abstract: learns Cartesian object velocity from single-frame oriented boxes without velocity labels by shifting predictions in time with predicted velocities on unlabeled frames; Doppler-derived pseudo labels only bootstrap the pretraining and an explicit radial-velocity module is an input; nuScenes; nearly matches fully supervised velocity and beats a radial-velocity-label baseline (no numbers on the page).
idea: time-shift consistency of detections as a velocity label

title: RaTrack: Moving Object Detection and Tracking with 4D Radar Point Cloud (ICRA 2024)
text: 4D radar on View-of-Delft: motion segmentation and clustering with a motion estimation module instead of boxes and classes; superior tracking precision for moving objects (abstract via search result; no numbers read). Point-based.

title: RICCARDO: Radar Hit Prediction and Convolution for Camera-Radar 3D Object Detection (CVPR 2025)
text: Models the distribution of radar hits around a detection (depends on category size orientation) predicted from a monocular detector and uses it as a matching kernel on measured radar points plus a fusion stage; state-of-the-art radar-camera on nuScenes (abstract via search result). A learned radar likelihood but position only no Doppler.
idea: predicted hit-distribution kernel as likelihood

title: TEOcc: Radar-camera Multi-modal Occupancy Prediction via Temporal Enhancement (ECAI 2024)
text: Abstract: training-only temporal branch that drops a frame and predicts its occupancy from adjacent frames; discarded at inference; state of the art on nuScenes claimed; no numbers on the page.

title: 4DRC-OCC: Robust Semantic Occupancy Prediction Through Fusion of 4D Radar and Camera (2026)
text: Abstract: first study of 4D radar plus camera for 3D semantic occupancy; automatically labelled dataset; no numbers on the page.

title: CaRLi-V: Camera-RADAR-LiDAR Point-Wise 3D Velocity Estimation
text: Abstract: velocity cube from raw radar radial velocity plus camera optical flow for the tangential part and lidar range in a closed form per point; custom data; open-source ROS2 package; no numbers on the page.
idea: radial from Doppler + tangential from flow in closed form
code: ROS2 package (no URL on the page)

title: Occ3D: A Large-Scale 3D Occupancy Prediction Benchmark for Autonomous Driving (NeurIPS 2023)
text: Released lidar-derived voxel labels for the 850 nuScenes trainval scenes at 2 Hz (28130 train + 6019 val keyframes): 200 x 200 x 16 voxels of 0.4 m over x y [-40 40] m and z [-1 5.4] m, 17 semantic classes + free, per frame semantics + mask_lidar + mask_camera. Made by static accumulation in the world frame and dynamic objects in box frames, VDBFusion mesh, lidar and camera ray-casting visibility. Trainval folder about 32 GB incl. images (gts alone not stated); MIT, nuScenes terms apply. Stops at 40 m: covers 66.7 % of our 60 m grid.
idea: static-structure layer (barrier manmade vegetation + parked boxes) cut from released labels without downloading lidar; use mask_lidar not mask_camera
licence: MIT (data + generation code); nuScenes CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 applies

title: SurroundOcc: Multi-Camera 3D Occupancy Prediction for Autonomous Driving (ICCV 2023)
text: Dense nuScenes occupancy labels from boxes + lidar semantics: movable objects and static scene stitched separately, Poisson meshing, nearest-neighbour semantics; 0.5 m voxels over x y [-50 50] m and z [-5 3] m (200 x 200 x 16, 16 classes + empty). Same 0.5 m grid as ours and reaches x = 50 m (83 % of our area). Radar-on gain in OccFusion on these labels: manmade 11.49 -> 16.16 vegetation 18.47 -> 21.81 barrier 18.39 -> 20.46 IoU. Data on Baidu Pan (size not stated); mesh vertices released; no visibility mask.
idea: 0.5 m aligned dense static labels to 50 m; generation script as the fallback recipe

title: OpenOccupancy: A Large Scale Benchmark for Surrounding Semantic Occupancy Perception (ICCV 2023)
text: nuScenes-Occupancy: 0.2 m voxels over x y [-51.2 51.2] m and z [-5 3] m (512 x 512 x 40; 16 classes + empty) for 850 scenes / 34 K keyframes; lidar superposition (static in world frame, objects via boxes) then pseudo-label fill of empty voxels then about 4000 human hours of purification. v0.1 archive about 5 GB, about 130 GB unpacked (Google Drive and Baidu).
idea: finest and longest-range released static labels; collapse 0.2 m to 0.5 m

title: Scene as Occupancy (OccNet) and the OpenOcc labels with flow (ICCV 2023)
text: OpenOcc: nuScenes occupancy built like Occ3D with per-voxel flow from box velocity for 8 movable classes (moving above 0.2 m/s). Paper grid 0.5 m +-50 m lidar frame, repo v2.1 grid 0.4 m +-40 m (labels.npz semantics + flow); openocc_v2.1.zip + infos.zip on OpenDataLab / Google Drive, size not stated; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
idea: flow = 0 on movable classes gives parked vs moving; we already have this from boxes

title: UniOcc: A Unified Benchmark for Occupancy Forecasting and Prediction in Autonomous Driving (2025)
text: Hugging Face dataset tasl-lab/uniocc re-packs nuScenes occupancy in three variants (Occ3D, OpenOccupancy, SurroundOcc) at 2 Hz with forward and backward voxel flow (L x W x H x 3 in voxels); 776 GB in total, per-folder sizes not shown; card says MIT.
idea: an open mirror of the three label sets if Google Drive or Baidu are unreachable

title: OccFusion: Multi-Sensor Fusion Framework for 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction
text: Camera + 5 radars (+ lidar) occupancy on nuScenes; no radar-specific loss (focal + Lovasz + scene-class affinity at four levels). Radar on SurroundOcc labels, IoU camera -> camera + radar: barrier 18.39 -> 20.46, manmade 11.49 -> 16.16, vegetation 18.47 -> 21.81, mIoU 18.88 -> 20.73. On Occ3D labels radar lowers the result; the authors blame the label range and the visibility mask.
idea: target classes for a radar-visible static map are manmade vegetation barrier; do not supervise radar with a 40 m / camera-masked label

title: REOcc: Camera-Radar Fusion with Radar Feature Enrichment for 3D Occupancy Prediction
text: Camera-radar occupancy on Occ3D-nuScenes; Radar Densifier is a fixed RCS-controlled Gaussian sharing between pillars, Radar Amplifier an MLP channel softmax; no radar-specific loss named. mIoU +5.46 over camera-only (dynamic classes +6.46: densifier +1.99 amplifier +1.72); no static-class numbers.
idea: parameter-free RCS-spread densifier for sparse radar pillars

title: MetaOcc: Surround-View 4D Radar and Camera Fusion Framework for 3D Occupancy Prediction
text: 4D-radar + camera occupancy on OmniHD-Scenes (manual lidar-point static annotation) and SurroundOcc-nuScenes; the radar branch has no direct supervision, loss = CE 1 + Lovasz 5 + geometric affinity 1 + semantic affinity 1; pseudo labels from Grounded-SAM + lidar + boxes supervise the occupancy output as a whole.
idea: confirms radar trained only through the shared occupancy loss

title: Doracamom: Joint 3D Detection and Occupancy Prediction with Multi-view 4D Radars and Cameras
text: Detection + occupancy from 4D radar and cameras; losses: detection (focal + L1), occupancy (CE + two affinity terms) and two auxiliary terms: BEV foreground mask from projected boxes (BCE + Dice) and binary occupied map derived from the semantic occupancy labels (BCE + Dice). RadarPillarNet has no own loss; auxiliary terms act on shared features.
idea: auxiliary binary occupied map from dense labels with BCE + Dice, as planned in 8.4

title: Road Boundary Detection Using 4D mmWave Radar for Autonomous Driving (4DRadarRBD)
text: Radar point-wise road-boundary segmentation + curve fit on 30424 own radar frames; labels inferred from lidar (PointPillars), no map labels. Accuracy 93 % overall; median Chamfer 0.023 m, median Hausdorff 2.34 m; no F1; no split by guardrail / curb / wall.
idea: radar boundary targets in the literature are lidar-built; test a map proxy on own data

title: nuScenes map expansion layers and the BEVFusion static-GT recipe (devkit data facts)
text: Polygon layers drivable_area road_segment road_block lane ped_crossing walkway stop_line carpark_area; line layers road_divider lane_divider traffic_light; no curb / guard rail / barrier / fence / wall layer. BEVFusion LoadBEVSegmentation: drivable_area* = road_segment + lane, divider = road_divider + lane_divider, others by layer name; no radar-specific map target in any fusion network read.
idea: map edges are a road-boundary prior, not a radar measurement; measure the proxy against static radar returns first

title: CaR1: A Multi-Modal Baseline for BEV Vehicle Segmentation via Camera-Radar Fusion
text: nuScenes camera-radar BEV vehicle segmentation; supervision only vehicle masks from projected boxes (BCE on main and auxiliary heads + Dice on the output head); vehicles under 40 % visibility excluded from evaluation; no radar-specific target.
idea: none
